Accountable obligation owner.value: Product Compliance owns the rate-filing determination for every base rate, factor, tier, territory, rating rule and manual page change; prior-approval and exemption calls escalate to Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Alabama rating law (ALDOI rate-filing statute, filed via SERFF) re-read at determination time as the representative cite, plus the current SERFF Filing Rules entry for each affected state; supporting cites re-read for Arizona, California (prior-approval rating law) and Connecticut

In-scope processes.value: Pricing rate indication approval to rate-filing determination gate: base rate level changes, factor and relativity revisions, tier and territory definitions, rating manual pages and rate-bearing underwriting rules, across all 51 jurisdictions and every writing company

In-scope systems.value: Earnix rate program change list is the source of rate elements; SERFF Filing Rules supplies the per-state review method; determinations are written to the filing determination log

Compliance procedure documented.value: Rate Filing Determination Procedure - indication intake, decomposition into rate elements, per-state review-method lookup, statewide rate level impact capture, deemer arithmetic, exemption basis and log entry before any rate is coded

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved jointly by the Head of Pricing and the Head of Compliance; re-approved annually and on any state rating bulletin (for example an ALDOI rate-filing bulletin or a California prior-approval regulation amendment)

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing / pre-use gate - the source text states no fixed calendar deadline, so the binding date is the latest submission date computed backwards from the target rate effective date using each state's review period and deemer days

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker milestone alerts at T-120, T-90, T-60 and T-30 days to the target rate effective date on every open determination; prior-approval states (California and the other prior-approval jurisdictions on the review-method matrix) alert from T-180

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Determination worksheet, dated per-state SERFF filing-rules captures, the signed statewide rate level impact schedule from Pricing and counsel sign-offs, retained 7 years from withdrawal of the rate

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any rate element effective in a state with no determination pre-dating its effective date is raised as a compliance exception with root cause, a self-report assessment and a remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs every no-filing-required call and every late or unfiled rate remediation before the determination log row can close

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every rate, factor, tier, territory, rating rule and manual page change with a rate effective date inside the quarter, taken from the Earnix rate program release log and the policy admin rate-table effective dating, split by writing company and state

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - any rate element in force without a determination dated before its effective date is a fail; one or more fails in a prior-approval state escalates to the Chief Actuary and the Head of Compliance within 5 business days

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is per filing, so the test runs quarterly across that quarter's rate effective dates, taking 100% of prior-approval-state rows and a sample of file-and-use rows

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside Product Compliance and Pricing and must have authored or reviewed none of the sampled rate determinations

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly rate-filing determination workpaper (population extract, reconciliation to the rate release log, sample selection, re-performance notes, exception list) filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-002

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Determination log export with per-state review method, statutory cite, SERFF tracking number and disposition date, producible for an ALDOI or other department rate examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Affairs Manager owns the department inquiry and single point of contact; Regulatory Counsel clears any statement conceding an unfiled or late rate before it leaves the company

checklist.step: Take in the approved rate indication and open a determination worksheet
actions: Collect from the Pricing Actuary the signed rate indication pack and, in Earnix, open Rate Programs and list every program version flagged Ready for filing.
Start a determination worksheet capturing writing company and NAIC co-code, line of business, TOI/Sub-TOI, target rate effective date for new business and for renewals, and the state list.

Ask the Head of Pricing for the hard date driver (loss-ratio deterioration, competitor move, reinsurance renewal) and record it, because it sets how much prior-approval review time the plan can absorb.
Name the folder <company>-<line>-rate-<target effective date> in the compliance evidence repository and attach the signed indication pack.
checklist.done: the worksheet carries company, line, TOI/Sub-TOI, both effective dates and the state list, with the signed indication attached.

checklist.step: Decompose the change into individually filable rate elements
actions: In Earnix compare the candidate rate program version against the in-force version and export the change report.
Give every changed object its own worksheet row and tag it BASE RATE, FACTOR/RELATIVITY, TIER, TERRITORY, RATING RULE, MANUAL PAGE or NON-RATE (agent communication, internal guideline).
For each row record the current value, the proposed value and the rating algorithm step it sits in, so a reviewer can see where in the calculation the change bites.
Flag any new rating variable (a factor not previously filed in that state) separately - new variables usually pull the whole filing into a longer review track.
Hand the tagged list back to the Product Filing Specialist with a written confirmation that nothing rate-bearing was tagged NON-RATE.
checklist.done: every changed rate object has its own row, a tag, current and proposed values, and new rating variables are flagged.

checklist.step: Quantify statewide rate level impact and policyholder disruption per state
actions: Run the rate change through the in-force book by state and produce overall statewide rate level impact percentage, premium impact in dollars and policy counts affected.
Produce the disruption distribution per state: percentage of policies moving more than +10%, more than +25% and more than the state's published disruption cap where one exists.
Record the number of policyholders and written premium affected in each state on the corresponding worksheet rows.
Sign the rate level impact schedule and email it to the Product Filing Specialist; the emailed figures are the ones that will be certified to the department.
Flag any state where the statewide impact exceeds the state's flex-band or prior-approval trigger threshold.
checklist.done: each state row carries a signed statewide rate level impact percentage, dollar impact, policy count and disruption distribution.

checklist.step: Read each affected state's current SERFF rate filing rules
actions: Log in to SERFF at login.serff.com with the company instance and your industry user id.
Open Industry then Filing Rules, select the state, Business Type Property and Casualty (or Life/Health as applicable), and the TOI/Sub-TOI that matches the product.
Read the state General Instructions and the Rate Filing requirements tab, including any attached rate filing checklist, rate data form and required supporting-documentation list.
Print the instructions to PDF as <state>-rate-filing-rules-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and save it to the determination folder - this dated capture is the evidence behind the review-method call.
Note every bulletin the instructions reference and open it; Alabama, Arizona, California and Connecticut all carry rate-specific bulletins that override the general text.
Repeat state by state until all 51 jurisdictions in scope are captured.
checklist.done: a dated rate-filing-rules capture and bulletin list exists in the folder for every affected jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Record the rate review method for each state and element
actions: Set the review method on each state/element row: PRIOR APPROVAL, FILE-AND-USE, USE-AND-FILE, FLEX RATING (within band), INFORMATIONAL or NOT SUBJECT TO FILING.

Paste into the row the exact sentence from the state instructions plus the rating statute or bulletin cite relied on - for the representative state that is the Alabama rate-filing statute administered by ALDOI.
Where the impact exceeds a flex band, reclassify the row to PRIOR APPROVAL and record the band and the tested impact percentage side by side.
Where the instructions are silent, email the state's SERFF contact listed on the state SERFF page and log the question, the date sent and the answer received on the row.
Highlight every PRIOR APPROVAL row - these set the critical path for the whole rate release.
checklist.done: every state/element row shows a review method, a quoted source sentence, a statutory cite and, where relevant, the flex band tested against.

checklist.step: Confirm product coding and the rate data forms each state demands
actions: Open the NAIC Uniform Product Coding Matrix for the line and pick the TOI and Sub-TOI that match the product being repriced.
Confirm on the state's SERFF Filing Rules page that the TOI is accepted through SERFF for Rate/Rule filing types, and note whether Rate and Rule must be filed together or separately.
Record the state's required rate data artifact on each row - the Rate/Rule Schedule tab entries, the state rate summary or expense exhibit form, and any statistical exhibit the instructions name.
Where a state takes rates outside SERFF, record the alternate portal URL or paper filing address and its own submission instructions.
checklist.done: TOI, Sub-TOI, filing type and the required rate data artifacts are recorded for every state and agree with the coding matrix.

checklist.step: Test each state against rate caps, flex bands and trigger thresholds
actions: For each state, read from the captured instructions any threshold that changes the review track: flex band percentage, disruption cap, new-variable rule or minimum data-volume requirement.
Compare the state's signed statewide rate level impact against that threshold and write the comparison on the row as tested value versus threshold.
Where the impact sits within a few points of a trigger, ask Pricing whether the change can be phased over two effective dates and record the decision.
Escalate to the Chief Actuary any state where the indicated rate exceeds what the state has historically approved, so the filed rate is set deliberately rather than discovered at objection stage.
checklist.done: every state row shows the tested impact against the state threshold and any phasing decision is recorded.

checklist.step: Support every not-subject-to-filing call with a named exemption
actions: Take each NOT SUBJECT TO FILING row and name the basis: exempt commercial purchaser or large-risk exemption, surplus lines, an inland marine class the state does not rate-regulate, or a genuinely non-rate item.
Paste the statute, regulation or bulletin granting the exemption together with its effective date into the row.
Where the exemption depends on a premium size or insured net-worth threshold, record the tested value and the system report it came from.
Reject any row whose only support is the phrase not required and send it back for a citation the same day.
checklist.done: every exempt row carries a named exemption, a dated citation, a tested threshold value where applicable and a counsel initial.

checklist.step: Search SERFF Filing Access for the rate filing currently approved in each state
actions: In SERFF open Filing Access and search by company name or NAIC co-code, state, TOI and filing type Rate.
Filter Disposition to Approved or Filed and sort by disposition date descending to find the rate filing currently in force in that state.

Open the most recent approved filing and record its SERFF Tracking Number, disposition date and approved rate effective date on the worksheet row - this is the baseline the new filing must be measured against.
Compare the approved rate pages to the proposed pages and confirm the change described in the worksheet is the only delta.
Note any prior objection letters on that filing; the same examiner usually raises the same questions again.
checklist.done: each state row names the currently approved SERFF tracking number, its disposition date and the confirmed delta to the proposed rates.

checklist.step: Compute the deemer clock and the latest submission date for each state
actions: Read the statutory review period or deemer days from the captured state instructions (commonly 30, 45, 60 or 90 days for rate filings) and write it on the row.
Add the objection-response allowance (10 business days as the working assumption) and any statutory clock suspension the state applies while an objection is open.
Compute latest submission date = target rate effective date minus (deemer days + objection allowance + rating system implementation lead) and write it on the row.
Load each latest submission date into the filing calendar and set T-120, T-90, T-60 and T-30 reminders against the target rate effective date, with T-180 for prior-approval states.
Report to the Insurance Product Manager any state whose latest submission date has already passed.
checklist.done: every state row carries deemer days, the computed latest submission date and a calendar entry with reminders set.

checklist.step: Fix the package scope by listing each state's companion rate requirements
actions: From each state rate filing checklist, list the companion items: actuarial memorandum and certification, loss and expense exhibits, trend and loss development support, credibility standard, investment income offset, expense provision, rate/rule schedule and the state rate summary form.
Name the owner and the due date for each companion item and hand them to Pricing, Actuarial or Legal.
Flag long-lead items now - California-style prior-approval templates, expense call data and any state-mandated statistical exhibit take weeks, not days.
Confirm with the Product Filing Specialist that every companion item is due before the state's latest submission date.
checklist.done: each state has a companion-item list with a named owner and a due date earlier than that state's latest submission date.

checklist.step: Write the determination rows into the Filing Determination Log
actions: Add one log row per state per rate element with: change id, writing company, state, element type, filing required Y/N, review method, filing type, statutory cite, statewide rate level impact, deemer days, latest submission date, decider and decision date.
Link each row to the determination folder holding the dated filing-rules captures and the signed rate level impact schedule.
Set row status to Determined - pending counsel where sign-off is needed, otherwise Determined - closed.
Run the log completeness report and clear every blank field before the pricing release freeze.
checklist.done: the log holds one complete, source-linked row per state per rate element with no blank fields.

checklist.step: Get Regulatory Counsel sign-off on prior-approval and exempt rows
actions: Route to counsel every PRIOR APPROVAL row and every NOT SUBJECT TO FILING row before the log closes.
Re-read the cited rating statute or bulletin as it currently reads and confirm or overturn the call in writing on the row.
Send overturned rows back to the Regulatory Filing Specialist for rework inside the same week so the latest submission date survives.
Stamp confirmed rows with counsel name and date and move them to Determined - closed.
checklist.done: no prior-approval or exempt row is closed without a dated written counsel confirmation.

checklist.step: Publish the determination to the release plan and arm the pre-use gate
actions: Attach the determination summary to the rate change record and circulate it to Pricing, Underwriting and the rating system configuration team.
Set the pre-use gate on every prior-approval state: no rate, factor or manual page may be effective in that state until an approval or a satisfied deemer is recorded.
Give the configuration team the per-state earliest-use dates so rate tables are effective-dated rather than released on a single national date.
Add each state's latest submission date and target effective date to the product release plan as tracked milestones.
checklist.done: the rate change record shows a per-state earliest-use date and every prior-approval state is blocked in the release plan.

checklist.step: File the determination evidence under the retention rule
actions: Move the determination folder - worksheet, dated filing-rules captures, rate level impact schedule, counsel sign-offs, calendar exports - into the compliance evidence repository under REG-002 and the rate effective date.
Apply the 7-year-from-rate-withdrawal retention label so the record outlives the rate itself.
Index the record so it is searchable by state, writing company, SERFF tracking number and rate effective date.
Confirm read access for Internal Audit and Regulatory Counsel and write access limited to Product Compliance.
checklist.done: the determination record is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by state, company and SERFF tracking number.

testing.step: Build the population of rate elements that took effect in the quarter
actions: Extract from the policy administration rate tables every rate, factor, tier, territory and manual page version with an effective date inside the quarter, by writing company and state.
Add the Earnix rate program release log and the rating engine deployment records so a change made only in configuration cannot hide from the extract.
Reconcile the two extracts row for row and resolve every difference with the Configuration Engineer before drawing a sample.
Have the extractor sign the population as complete and record the extract query and run date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a single reconciled population exists, signed as complete, with the extract query recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile every in-force rate element to a determination that pre-dates it
actions: Match each population row to a Filing Determination Log row on change id plus state plus element type.
Confirm the determination decision date is strictly earlier than the rate effective date.
List unmatched rows and determinations dated on or after the effective date as automatic exceptions - no judgement is applied at this step.
Quantify the written premium sitting behind each unmatched row so the exception carries a size, not just a count.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a pre-dated determination or listed as an exception with its premium exposure.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of rows in prior-approval states and 100% of rows carrying a new rating variable.
Take 25 further rows by seeded random selection from the remaining population, with a minimum total sample of 40 rows.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Confirm the sample spans at least three writing companies and both new-business and renewal effective dates.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all prior-approval and new-variable rows, and its selection basis is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the review-method call in SERFF for each sampled row
actions: Open SERFF Industry then Filing Rules for the sampled state and TOI, and read the General Instructions and Rate Filing requirements without first reading the determination worksheet.
Reach your own conclusion on prior approval versus file-and-use versus flex band and write it down before opening the log row.
Compare the two; any difference is an exception, including a right answer supported by the wrong citation.
Screenshot the instructions page relied on into the workpaper with the date it was read.
testing.done: each sampled row carries an independent re-performance conclusion and a dated source capture.

testing.step: Re-perform the statewide rate level impact behind the review-method call
actions: For each sampled state, recompute the statewide rate level impact from the in-force premium extract and the old and new rate factors.
Compare your figure to the signed rate level impact schedule Pricing certified and record the difference in percentage points.
Where the recomputed impact crosses the state flex band or prior-approval trigger but the recorded impact did not, raise it as a misclassification exception.
Tie the recomputed impact to the figure actually certified in the filing so the number filed with the department is the number tested.
testing.done: recomputed rate level impacts agree with the certified schedule within tolerance, or the difference is raised as a misclassification.

testing.step: Test the support behind every not-subject-to-filing row in the sample
actions: Pull each exempt sampled row and read the cited rating statute, regulation or bulletin as it read on the determination date.
Confirm the exemption actually reaches the element filed under it, including any premium size or net-worth threshold and the tested value.
Confirm a dated counsel sign-off exists and pre-dates the rate effective date.
Treat an uncited not required as a control failure rather than a documentation gap.
testing.done: every exempt sampled row is supported by a verified citation, a tested threshold and a counsel sign-off dated before the rate went into effect.

testing.step: Trace every filing-required row to a real SERFF rate filing
actions: In SERFF Filing Access, search the SERFF Tracking Number recorded on the sampled row.
Confirm the filing exists for the right writing company, state, TOI and filing type, and that the rate pages attached match the elements in the population row.
Read the submission date and the disposition (Filed, Approved, Closed) and compare both to the rate effective date in policy admin.
Capture the SERFF filing detail screen and the disposition letter into the workpaper as the traced evidence.
testing.done: every filing-required sampled row traces to an identified SERFF filing whose disposition and dates are captured.

testing.step: Recompute the deemer arithmetic and prove the pre-use gate held
actions: For 10 sampled prior-approval rows, recompute latest submission date = rate effective date minus (deemer days + objection allowance + implementation lead) using the deemer days printed in the state instructions.
Compare the actual SERFF submission date to the recomputed date and record every filing submitted later than its own deadline.
Check the policy admin rate-table effective date is on or after the approval date or the date the deemer was satisfied.
Treat any premium charged on an unapproved rate as a reportable breach with a premium-refund exposure estimate, not as a test exception.
testing.done: no sampled state charged a rate before approval or a satisfied deemer, and every deemer computation reconciles.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception carrying change id, state, element, what was missed, premium exposure and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: change not intaken, wrong TOI, stale filing rules, impact misstated, timeline compressed, configuration released early.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for any premium charged on an unapproved rate open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel within 5 business days.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, a named owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-unfiled-rate threshold and split it between prior-approval and file-and-use states.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with direct references to the workpaper evidence behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored none of the sampled determinations, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any use-before-approval breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper under REG-002.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the content and actuarial defensibility of the rate filing package; the Product Filing Specialist owns package assembly and the state checklist certification

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - the supporting-documentation requirements are taken from each state's current SERFF rate filing checklist rather than memory, with the Alabama rate-filing statute and ALDOI checklist as the representative source and Arizona, California and Connecticut checklists re-read for the same release

In-scope processes.value: Package assembly for a rate filing: actuarial memorandum and certification, indication and experience exhibits, trend and loss development support, expense and investment income provisions, rate/rule schedule, manual page redlines, transmittal and state rate summary forms

In-scope systems.value: Indication and exhibit numbers are produced in the actuarial platform; the assembled package baseline is version-controlled in the document management repository before submission

Compliance procedure documented.value: Rate Filing Package Preparation Procedure - checklist harvest per state, exhibit build, actuarial memorandum drafting and certification, legal review of rating variables, fee and attachment standards, package QC before handover to submission

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary for actuarial content and the Head of Compliance for the checklist certification step; refreshed whenever a state reissues its rate filing checklist

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing - the package must be complete and QC-passed at least 5 business days before that state's latest submission date, so a rejected attachment does not consume the deemer runway

Deadline reminders configured.value: Package milestone reminders in the filing tracker at package-start, exhibits-due, memo-due, legal-review-due and QC-due, each dated backwards from the state's latest submission date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The exact package baseline submitted - memorandum, exhibits, manual pages, transmittal, checklist certification and fee receipt - retained 7 years from rate withdrawal with a hash or version stamp proving it is what went to the department

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any package submitted missing a checklist-required exhibit, or an exhibit whose numbers differ from the certified indication, is logged as an exception with the resulting objection or rejection recorded against it

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Chief Actuary signs off any restatement of a filed exhibit or a corrected actuarial memorandum before it is refiled

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every rate filing package handed to submission during the quarter, across all writing companies and states, taken from the filing tracker package register

Pass/fail thresholds.value: A package fails if any state-checklist-required item is absent, if an exhibit figure disagrees with the certified indication, or if the certification page is unsigned or undated; more than 5% of packages failing, or any unsigned certification, escalates to the Chief Actuary

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is per filing; testing runs quarterly over that quarter's packages, with every package that drew a completeness objection reviewed at 100%

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Peer reviewer must be an actuary who did not build the indication or the exhibits under test; final sign-off sits with the Chief Actuary

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly package-completeness workpaper - checklist-to-package mapping, exhibit tie-out, certification inspection, exception list - in the compliance evidence repository under REG-002

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The submitted package baseline plus the completed state checklist and the exhibit tie-out schedule, reproducible on request during a rate examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Content questions on the package route to the Product / Filing Actuary through the Regulatory Filing Specialist; only the Regulatory Filing Specialist replies inside SERFF, and Regulatory Counsel clears any revision to a certified figure

checklist.step: Harvest the current filing checklist for every state in the release
actions: In SERFF open Industry then Filing Rules, select the state and the TOI/Sub-TOI, and download the state's rate filing checklist and supporting-documentation requirements.
Convert each checklist into a package build sheet with one row per required item and columns for owner, due date and status.
Compare this release's checklist against the version used on the previous filing for the same state and highlight new or changed requirements.
Send each build sheet to the Product / Filing Actuary and the Product Filing Specialist and store it in the filing folder as <state>-checklist-<yyyy-mm-dd>.
checklist.done: every state in the release has a dated build sheet with one row per checklist requirement and an owner against each.

checklist.step: Build the rate indication and experience exhibits
actions: Produce the statewide indication exhibit showing earned premium at present rates, developed and trended incurred losses, LAE, the permissible loss ratio and the indicated rate change.
Attach the experience exhibits: earned premium and incurred loss by accident year for the experience period the state requires, with the number of years stated.
Number every exhibit and add a cross-reference column showing which checklist row it satisfies.
Lock the underlying model version and record its identifier on the exhibit cover page so the numbers can be reproduced.
Hand the exhibit set to the Product / Filing Actuary with the data-as-of date stated.
checklist.done: a numbered, cross-referenced indication and experience exhibit set exists with a locked model version and a stated data-as-of date.

checklist.step: Build the trend, loss development and credibility support
actions: Produce loss development triangles and the selected age-to-age and tail factors, showing both the fitted and the selected factor with the reason for any deviation.
Produce the frequency and severity trend exhibit with the fitted period, the fit method and the selected annual trend, and state the trend-from and trend-to dates.
Document the credibility standard applied, the full-credibility volume, the actual volume and the complement of credibility used.
Where the state prescribes its own standard (a mandated credibility volume or a capped trend), show both the company selection and the state-prescribed figure.
Send the pack to the Pricing Actuary for consistency with the indication exhibit before it goes into the package.
checklist.done: development, trend and credibility exhibits exist with selections, sources and any state-prescribed alternative shown side by side.

checklist.step: Build the expense provision and investment income exhibits
actions: Pull the countrywide expense ratios from the general ledger by expense category - commission and brokerage, other acquisition, general expense, taxes licenses and fees - for the years the state requires.
Reconcile the expense ratios to the filed Insurance Expense Exhibit so the department sees the same numbers it already holds.
Compute the underwriting profit provision and, where the state requires it, the investment income offset with the yield assumption and its source stated.
Ask Finance to confirm in writing that the ledger figures are final for the periods used, and file the confirmation.
checklist.done: expense, profit and investment income exhibits tie to the ledger and to the Insurance Expense Exhibit, with a written Finance confirmation on file.

checklist.step: Draft the actuarial memorandum and prepare the certification
actions: Write the memorandum in the order the state checklist asks for: purpose and scope, proposed effective dates for new and renewal business, overall statewide rate level change, data and experience period, development, trend, expense and profit provisions, credibility, changes to rating variables, and the disruption analysis.
State the overall statewide rate level change figure exactly as it appears on the signed rate level impact schedule - one number, used identically everywhere in the package.

Prepare the certification page naming the qualified actuary, the qualification standard relied on, and the statement that the rates are not excessive, inadequate or unfairly discriminatory as required by the state rating law.
Have the qualified actuary sign and date the certification; an unsigned certification blocks the whole submission.
Cross-reference every memorandum section to its supporting exhibit number.
checklist.done: a signed, dated actuarial memorandum and certification exists whose stated rate level change matches the signed impact schedule exactly.

checklist.step: Assemble the rate and rule schedule and the manual page redlines
actions: Produce the new manual pages with page numbers and edition dates printed in the footer of every page.
Produce a redline of each manual page against the currently approved edition, using the edition retrieved from the approved SERFF filing rather than an internal draft.
Build the rate/rule schedule listing each rate or rule item, its previous rate reference, its new rate reference and whether it is New, Replacement or Withdrawn.
Confirm every element on the determination worksheet appears on the schedule and that nothing appears on the schedule that was never determined.
Save the set as the package baseline with a version number in the document repository.
checklist.done: manual pages, redlines against the approved edition and a complete rate/rule schedule are baselined and reconcile item for item to the determination worksheet.

checklist.step: Complete the transmittal and the state rate data forms
actions: Complete the Uniform Transmittal Document or the state's own transmittal with company name, NAIC group and company codes, TOI/Sub-TOI, filing type, effective dates and the company contact.

Fill the SERFF Rate/Rule Schedule tab entries and the state rate summary form - written premium, policy counts, current and proposed rate level, expiring effective date and last filing tracking number.
Enter the overall percentage rate impact and the number of policyholders affected in the SERFF Rate Information section so the SERFF fields match the memorandum.
Check every number entered against the signed rate level impact schedule before saving the form.
checklist.done: transmittal and rate data forms are complete and every figure on them matches the signed impact schedule and the memorandum.

checklist.step: Draft the cover letter for the state
actions: Write a one-page cover letter naming the company, the line, the requested effective dates for new and renewal business, and the overall statewide rate level change.
Say plainly what is changing and why, and list the enclosures against the state checklist rows.
Where the state requires it, include the statement that the filing is submitted under the state prior-approval or file-and-use rating law and quote that cite.
Name the filing contact and direct phone number the examiner should use for objections.
checklist.done: the cover letter states the requested effective dates, the rate level change, the statutory basis and a named contact, and lists enclosures against the checklist.

checklist.step: Get independent actuarial peer review of the indication
actions: Assign a reviewing actuary who built none of the exhibits under review.
Have the reviewer re-derive the indicated change from the raw premium and loss data and compare it to the exhibit, documenting any difference.
Have the reviewer challenge the three selections that move the answer most - trend, tail development factor and profit provision - and record the challenge and the response.
Record the peer review conclusion and sign it; an unreviewed indication does not enter the package.
checklist.done: a signed peer review record exists showing an independent re-derivation and a documented challenge of the key selections.

checklist.step: Get legal review of rating variables and manual language
actions: Read every new or changed rating variable against the state's prohibited and restricted rating factor rules, including any restriction on credit-based scores, occupation, education, gender or ZIP-level territory definitions.
Read the manual page language for anything that could read as an unfiled underwriting rule or an unfair discrimination exposure.
Confirm the certification wording matches the wording the state rating law requires.
Record approval, or required edits with a deadline, on the package build sheet.
checklist.done: every new or changed rating variable and manual page has a recorded legal disposition against the state's prohibited-factor rules.

checklist.step: Confirm the filing fee amount and payment route for each state
actions: Read the fee from the state's SERFF Filing Rules page - flat fee, per-form fee or per-rate-page fee - and record the amount on the build sheet.
Confirm whether the state takes SERFF EFT or requires a separate check or state portal payment, and record the route.
Where EFT applies, confirm with Finance that the SERFF EFT account is funded for the release's total fees.
Attach the fee confirmation or check request to the package folder.
checklist.done: each state has a recorded fee amount, a confirmed payment route and a funded payment ready before submission.

checklist.step: Bring the attachments up to the portal technical standard
actions: Convert every attachment to text-searchable PDF, remove DRAFT watermarks and confirm no tracked changes or comments survive in the file.
Keep each attachment under the SERFF per-attachment size guidance (about 3 MB) and split oversized exhibits by exhibit number rather than by page count.
Name every file to the state's convention where one exists, otherwise <state>-<company>-<exhibit number>-<short name>.pdf.
Provide any data file the state requires in the format it names (Excel workbook or delimited text) with a column dictionary tab.
checklist.done: every attachment is searchable, watermark-free, within the size cap and named to convention, with data files in the required format.

checklist.step: Certify the state checklist line by line
actions: Walk the state build sheet row by row and mark each requirement Included with the exhibit number, or Not applicable with the reason.
Complete and sign the state's own certification of compliance form where one exists.
Reject the package back to the owner for any row that is neither included nor justified - never submit against an open row.
Attach the completed checklist as the first document in the package so the examiner sees it first.
checklist.done: the state checklist is complete, signed, and every row is either mapped to an exhibit number or justified as not applicable.

checklist.step: Run package QC and hand over to submission
actions: Tie the overall rate level change across four places - memorandum, rate/rule schedule, SERFF rate information fields and cover letter - and stop the package on any mismatch.
Confirm the effective dates in the package match the determination worksheet and that they respect the state's latest submission date.
Confirm the certification page is signed and dated, the peer review record is attached and the legal disposition is closed.
Record the QC result and hand the baselined package to the Regulatory Filing Specialist for submission at least 5 business days before the latest submission date.
checklist.done: QC is recorded, the rate level change ties across all four documents, and the package is handed over ahead of the state deadline.

checklist.step: Baseline and retain the exact package that will be submitted
actions: Freeze the package version, record its version identifier and file it in the compliance evidence repository under REG-002, the state and the target effective date.
Apply the 7-year-from-rate-withdrawal retention label to the package and its build sheet.
Record which package version is going to which state, since states in the same release rarely receive identical packages.
Confirm the frozen version is read-only so a later edit cannot be mistaken for what was filed.
checklist.done: a frozen, read-only, retention-labelled package version is filed per state and mapped to the state it was submitted to.

testing.step: Build the population of rate filing packages prepared in the quarter
actions: Extract from the filing tracker every rate filing package handed to submission in the quarter with company, state, TOI, target effective date and package version.
Reconcile the extract to the SERFF submission list for the same period so a package that was submitted but never registered in the tracker is caught.
Add packages that were prepared and then withdrawn, since a withdrawn package still had to meet the checklist.
Sign the population as complete and record the extraction date.
testing.done: a reconciled package population exists, agreed to the SERFF submission list, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each package to the state checklist in force on its preparation date
actions: Retrieve the state's rate filing checklist as it stood on the package preparation date, not today's version.
Compare the checklist rows to the package contents list and mark any required item with no matching attachment.
Confirm the checklist certification stored with the package is the same version you retrieved.
Record missing items as automatic exceptions regardless of whether the state raised an objection.
testing.done: each package is mapped against the contemporaneous checklist and every unmatched requirement is listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of packages
actions: Take 100% of packages for prior-approval states and 100% of packages that drew a completeness objection or a rejection.
Take 10 further packages by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum total of 20 packages.
Record the seed, the population size, the stratification and the selection date in the workpaper.
Confirm the sample includes at least one package containing a new rating variable.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering all prior-approval and objected packages plus a random remainder.

testing.step: Tie the certified rate level change across the whole package
actions: For each sampled package, read the overall statewide rate level change from the actuarial memorandum, the cover letter, the rate/rule schedule and the SERFF Rate Information fields.
Compare all four to the signed rate level impact schedule from Pricing and record any difference to two decimal places.
Trace the figure back to the indication exhibit and confirm the exhibit arithmetic reproduces it.
Treat any disagreement as a fail, because the department relies on the certified figure.
testing.done: the certified rate level change agrees across memorandum, cover letter, schedule, SERFF fields and the impact schedule, or the difference is logged as a fail.

testing.step: Re-perform the indication on a sub-sample
actions: For three sampled packages, rebuild the indicated rate change from the raw earned premium at present rates, developed and trended losses, expense provision and permissible loss ratio.
Compare your indication to the filed exhibit and reconcile any difference to a named selection - trend, development tail, expense or credibility.
Check that the selections used in the filing match the peer review record and the model version stated on the exhibit cover page.
Document the re-performance arithmetic in the workpaper so a third party can follow it.
testing.done: the filed indication is independently reproduced on the sub-sample, with every difference reconciled to a named selection.

testing.step: Inspect the certification and peer review evidence
actions: Confirm each sampled package carries a certification page signed and dated by a named qualified actuary before the submission date.
Confirm the certification wording carries the not excessive, inadequate or unfairly discriminatory statement the state rating law requires.
Confirm a signed peer review record exists and that the reviewer built none of the exhibits.
Treat a certification signed after the submission date as a fail, not a filing-order technicality.
testing.done: every sampled package has a pre-dated signed certification with the statutory wording and an independent peer review record.

testing.step: Verify the legal disposition of new and changed rating variables
actions: For each sampled package containing a new or changed rating variable, confirm a recorded legal disposition exists dated before submission.
Re-read the state's prohibited and restricted rating factor rules as they stood at submission and confirm the variable was permissible in that state.
Check that any state-specific restriction (credit score use, territory definition, occupation or education) was applied rather than carried over from the countrywide design.
Log any variable filed without a disposition as a control failure with a self-assessment of exposure.
testing.done: every new or changed rating variable in the sample has a pre-dated legal disposition verified against the state's rules.

testing.step: Recompute package readiness against the state deadline
actions: For each sampled package, compare the QC completion date to the state's latest submission date recorded on the determination row.
Recompute that latest submission date from the state deemer days and the target effective date and confirm the recorded value is right.
Record any package that was QC-passed later than 5 business days before the deadline as a timeliness exception.
Correlate late QC against objections received, since late packages produce avoidable objections.
testing.done: every sampled package has a recomputed deadline and a recorded lead time, with late packages listed as timeliness exceptions.

testing.step: Log every package exception with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying company, state, package version, the missing or inconsistent item and the objection or rejection it produced.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: stale checklist used, exhibit not built, figure not tied, certification unsigned, legal review skipped, attachment standard breached.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and require a checklist or build-sheet change where the same cause has appeared twice.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the package test
actions: Compute the package failure rate against the 5% threshold and report unsigned certifications separately at zero tolerance.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the tie-out and re-performance evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared none of the sampled packages, sign the workpaper.
File the signed workpaper under REG-002 and report failure rate and trend to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, failure rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Submits every rate filing in SERFF or the state's own portal and owns the filing from Submitted to Closed, including tracking-number capture and disposition recording

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - the submission channel and filing type are taken from the state's current SERFF Filing Rules entry at submission time; the Alabama rate-filing statute administered by ALDOI is the representative basis and Arizona, California and Connecticut are confirmed as SERFF-accepting for the same TOI

In-scope processes.value: Submission and disposition tracking for rate filings: SERFF filing shell creation, schedule tabs and attachment upload, EFT fee payment, submission, status monitoring through Assigned, Pending Industry Response and Closed, and disposition capture

In-scope systems.value: SERFF is the system of record for submission and disposition; every SERFF tracking number and status change is mirrored into the internal filing tracker the same business day

Compliance procedure documented.value: Rate Filing Submission and Disposition Procedure - shell creation, schedule tab completion, attachment upload, fee payment, submit, daily status sweep, objection routing, disposition capture and closure

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance; reviewed annually and after any NAIC SERFF release that changes the industry interface or the rate information fields

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing - submission must occur on or before the state's computed latest submission date, and the deemer clock is tracked from the SERFF submission date forward using the state's statutory review period

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker alerts on the submission date itself, then at deemer day minus 15 and deemer day minus 5, plus a daily unactioned-status alert for any filing left in Pending Industry Response

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: SERFF filing receipt with tracking number, the submitted attachment list, the EFT fee confirmation, all correspondence and the final disposition letter, retained 7 years from rate withdrawal

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Filings submitted after the latest submission date, filings disapproved or withdrawn, and filings left without a captured disposition beyond the state review period are each logged as exceptions with disposition and owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late submission, every withdrawal-and-refile decision and every disapproved filing before the rate release plan is changed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All rate filings with a SERFF submission date inside the quarter plus all filings open at quarter end, by company and state, taken from the SERFF filing list and the internal tracker

Pass/fail thresholds.value: A filing fails if it was submitted after its latest submission date, if the SERFF tracking number is missing from the tracker, or if a closed filing has no captured disposition; any disapproval or expired-deemer-without-record escalates immediately to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is per filing; testing runs quarterly over the quarter's submissions, with a weekly operational status sweep between tests so aged filings surface before the test

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have submitted or responded to any sampled filing in SERFF

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly submission and disposition workpaper - SERFF filing list export, tracker reconciliation, timeliness recomputation, disposition tracing - in the compliance evidence repository under REG-002

Regulator-ready documentation.value: SERFF tracking number, submission date, disposition date and disposition letter for every filing, exportable as a state-by-state schedule for a department rate examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: All correspondence with the department stays inside the SERFF filing so the record is complete; the Regulatory Filing Specialist is the named filing contact and Regulatory Counsel clears any withdrawal or resubmission statement

checklist.step: Create the SERFF filing shell for the state
actions: In SERFF choose Create New Filing, select the state, Business Type, TOI, Sub-TOI and Filing Type Rate or Rate/Rule as the state's rules require.
Select the writing company from the company list and confirm the NAIC company code shown matches the company on the determination row.
Enter the filing description, the company tracking number from the internal filing tracker, and the requested effective dates for new business and renewal business.
Set the filing contact to the Regulatory Filing Specialist with direct phone and email, since objections arrive to this contact.
Save the shell and copy the SERFF Tracking Number straight into the internal filing tracker row.
checklist.done: a saved SERFF shell exists with the correct company, TOI, filing type and effective dates, and its tracking number is recorded internally.

checklist.step: Complete the Rate/Rule Schedule and Rate Information tabs
actions: On the Rate/Rule Schedule tab add one entry per rate or manual item with document name, exhibit or rule number, rate action New, Replacement or Withdrawn, and the previous state filing number where it is a replacement.

On the Rate Information tab enter the overall percentage rate impact, the written premium change, the number of policyholders affected, the maximum and minimum percentage change and the expiring effective date.
Copy each of these figures from the signed rate level impact schedule rather than retyping from the memorandum.
Where the state requires it, complete the state-specific rate summary or expense exhibit fields that appear on the Supporting Documentation tab.
checklist.done: schedule and rate information tabs are complete and every figure matches the signed rate level impact schedule.

checklist.step: Upload the package attachments to the correct schedule tabs
actions: Upload the manual pages and rate exhibits to the Rate/Rule Schedule tab, and the actuarial memorandum, exhibits, cover letter and completed state checklist to the Supporting Documentation tab.
Satisfy every Supporting Documentation item the state has pre-loaded, using Bypass with a written reason only where the item genuinely does not apply.
Open each uploaded PDF from inside SERFF to confirm it rendered and is the frozen package version, not a working copy.
Confirm the attachment count in SERFF equals the package contents list handed over by QC.
checklist.done: every package document is uploaded to the right tab, renders correctly in SERFF, and no supporting-documentation item is left unsatisfied without a written reason.

checklist.step: Pay the state filing fee through the SERFF EFT process
actions: Enter the fee amount on the SERFF filing fee section exactly as computed from the state's Filing Rules fee schedule.
Submit the EFT payment through SERFF where the state accepts it, or issue the check request to Accounts Payable with the state, company and SERFF tracking number on the request.
Confirm the SERFF filing shows the fee as paid before submitting, since several states reject unpaid rate filings without opening them.
Save the EFT confirmation into the filing folder against the tracking number.
checklist.done: the correct fee is paid by the state's accepted route and the confirmation is filed against the SERFF tracking number.

checklist.step: Run the pre-submission validation and submit the filing
actions: Run the SERFF filing validation and clear every error and every warning, recording the reason for any warning deliberately left.
Re-check the requested effective dates against the determination row so the filing does not request a date the deemer cannot reach.
Submit the filing to the state and capture the submission confirmation screen and the submission date and time.
Write the submission date, SERFF tracking number and state filing number (once assigned) into the internal filing tracker the same business day.
Notify the Insurance Product Manager that the state's deemer clock has started and give the computed decision-due date.
checklist.done: the filing is submitted with validation clear, and submission date and tracking number are recorded internally the same day.

checklist.step: Compute and record the state's decision-due date from the submission date
actions: Take the statutory review period from the captured state filing rules and add it to the SERFF submission date to get the decision-due or deemer date.
Record whether the state's clock pauses while an objection is open, because that changes the arithmetic later.
Write the decision-due date onto the tracker row and set alerts at decision-due minus 15 and minus 5 days.
Flag any filing whose decision-due date falls after the target rate effective date so the effective date can be moved before customers are quoted.
checklist.done: each submitted filing shows a computed decision-due date, its clock-pause rule, alerts and a flag where it cannot reach the target effective date.

checklist.step: Sweep filing status daily and act on state activity
actions: Each business day open the SERFF filing list filtered to the company instance and sort by Last Activity date.
Review every filing in Assigned, Pending Industry Response or Objection status and open any that changed since the previous sweep.
Route objections to the Product / Filing Actuary the same day with the state's response deadline stated in the handover.
Update the internal tracker status for every filing whose SERFF status changed and record who was notified.
checklist.done: the daily sweep is completed and every SERFF status change is mirrored to the tracker with an owner assigned the same day.

checklist.step: Escalate filings that go quiet past the state's review period
actions: List every filing where the decision-due date has passed with no disposition recorded in SERFF.
Send a status enquiry through the SERFF filing Note to Reviewer naming the tracking number, submission date and statutory review period.
Where the state's law provides for deemer approval, confirm with Regulatory Counsel in writing whether the deemer has been satisfied before anyone relies on it.
Record the enquiry, the reply and counsel's deemer opinion on the tracker row.
checklist.done: every overdue filing carries a dated state enquiry and, where deemer is claimed, a written counsel opinion.

checklist.step: Capture the disposition and the approved effective dates
actions: Open the Disposition tab of the closed filing and download the disposition letter or state acknowledgement.
Record the disposition status (Approved, Filed, Acknowledged, Disapproved, Withdrawn), the disposition date and the approved effective dates for new and renewal business.
Compare the approved effective dates to the dates requested; states frequently approve a later date than requested and the release plan must follow the approved date.
Attach the disposition letter to the tracker row and to the compliance evidence folder.
checklist.done: every closed filing has a downloaded disposition letter, a recorded status and the approved effective dates captured.

checklist.step: Reconcile approved content against what was submitted
actions: Open the disposition and compare the approved rate/rule schedule items against the items submitted, item by item.
Identify anything approved with modification, approved in part, or excluded, and mark the corresponding determination row.
Where the state approved a reduced rate change, get Pricing to confirm in writing which factors are being cut back and by how much.
Update the rate/rule schedule baseline to the approved version and mark the submitted version superseded.
checklist.done: the approved item list is reconciled to the submitted item list and every modification is written back to the determination row.

checklist.step: Handle disapprovals, withdrawals and refiling decisions
actions: Convene Pricing, Product and Regulatory Counsel within 3 business days of any disapproval or requested withdrawal.
Decide the route in writing: amend and refile, withdraw and refile at a lower indication, appeal through the state's hearing process, or drop the state from the release.
Where withdrawal is chosen, withdraw inside SERFF with a stated reason rather than letting the filing sit.
Record the decision, its owner and the new target dates on the tracker and inform the Insurance Product Manager.
checklist.done: every disapproval or withdrawal has a dated written decision with an owner and revised target dates.

checklist.step: Publish an approval notification to the downstream teams
actions: Send an approval notice naming the state, company, SERFF tracking number, disposition date, approved new-business effective date and approved renewal effective date.
Attach the approved rate pages and the disposition letter so the configuration team codes from the approved version, not the submitted one.
Copy Underwriting, Product and the rating configuration team, and require an acknowledgement from the configuration owner.
Record the notification date on the tracker row as the start of the implementation window.
checklist.done: an approval notice with approved dates and approved rate pages has been sent and acknowledged by the configuration owner.

checklist.step: Keep the internal tracker reconciled to SERFF weekly
actions: Export the SERFF filing list for the company instance and the internal tracker extract for the same period.
Match on SERFF tracking number and list filings present in one system and not the other in both directions.
Investigate each break with the Regulatory Filing Specialist and correct the tracker, never the reverse.
Record the weekly reconciliation result and the break count as evidence that the tracker is a reliable source for testing.
checklist.done: a weekly two-way reconciliation between SERFF and the tracker is completed with every break resolved and recorded.

checklist.step: Close the filing record only when disposition and dates are complete
actions: Before setting the tracker row to Closed, confirm the row carries tracking number, submission date, disposition status, disposition date, approved effective dates and the disposition letter.
Confirm the determination row and the rate release plan both show the approved effective dates rather than the requested ones.
Reject closure on any row with a blank disposition field.
Record the closer name and closing date.
checklist.done: no filing row is closed without a complete disposition record and approved dates written back to the determination and release plan.

checklist.step: Archive the full filing record including correspondence
actions: Export the complete SERFF filing including submitted attachments, all correspondence, objection letters, responses and the disposition, and file it under REG-002 by state and tracking number.
Apply the 7-year-from-rate-withdrawal retention label and confirm the record is read-only.
Index by SERFF tracking number, state filing number, company and approved effective date.
Confirm Internal Audit can retrieve the record without going through the filing team.
checklist.done: the full SERFF record including correspondence is archived, retention-labelled and independently retrievable by tracking number.

testing.step: Build the population of rate filings submitted or open in the quarter
actions: Export from SERFF the filing list for every company instance with submission dates inside the quarter, plus all filings still open at quarter end.
Export the internal filing tracker for the same period and match on SERFF tracking number.
List one-sided matches in both directions and resolve each with the Regulatory Filing Specialist before sampling.
Sign the reconciled population as complete and record both export dates.
testing.done: a two-way reconciled SERFF-to-tracker population exists, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile submitted filings back to approved determinations
actions: Match every submitted filing to a determination log row for the same company, state and rate elements.
List filings submitted with no determination on file, and determinations that required a filing with no submission, as exceptions in separate categories.
Confirm the filing type submitted (Rate, Rate/Rule) matches the review method recorded on the determination.
Quantify the in-force premium behind any determination with no submission.
testing.done: every submission is tied to a determination and every unfiled determination is listed with its premium exposure.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of filings
actions: Take 100% of filings in prior-approval states, 100% of disapprovals and withdrawals, and 100% of filings open past their decision-due date.
Take 20 further filings by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum total of 35.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
Confirm the sample covers at least four states and more than one writing company.
testing.done: a reproducible, stratified sample is drawn covering all high-risk filings plus a random remainder.

testing.step: Re-perform the submission-timeliness computation
actions: For each sampled filing, recompute the latest submission date from the state deemer days, objection allowance and implementation lead against the target effective date.
Compare the actual SERFF submission date to the recomputed date and record the days early or late.
Confirm the deemer days used come from the dated state filing-rules capture, not from the tracker's stored default.
List every filing submitted after its own latest submission date as a timeliness exception with the days late.
testing.done: each sampled filing has an independently recomputed deadline and a recorded days-early or days-late figure.

testing.step: Verify the SERFF rate information fields against the certified figures
actions: Open each sampled filing's Rate Information tab in SERFF and read the overall percentage rate impact, written premium change and policyholders affected.
Compare those values to the signed rate level impact schedule and to the actuarial memorandum.
Check the Rate/Rule Schedule entries list every element on the determination row with the right rate action and previous state filing number.
Capture the tab screens into the workpaper as evidence of what the state actually saw.
testing.done: the SERFF rate information and schedule entries agree with the certified figures and the determination, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Trace fee payment and validation clearance
actions: Confirm each sampled filing shows the fee paid before submission and that the amount matches the state's fee schedule as captured in the filing rules.
Trace the EFT confirmation or check request to the filing folder and to the ledger disbursement.
Confirm no filing was submitted with an unresolved validation error, and read the recorded reason for any warning left open.
List fee underpayments and unexplained warnings separately, since both cause avoidable state rejections.
testing.done: fee payment is traced to a confirmation and a ledger entry for every sampled filing, and validation exceptions are listed.

testing.step: Trace each closed filing to its captured disposition
actions: Open the Disposition tab in SERFF for each sampled closed filing and read the status, disposition date and approved effective dates.
Compare them to the tracker row and to the approval notification sent to the configuration team.
Confirm the disposition letter is stored in the evidence repository and is the same document SERFF holds.
Treat a closed filing with no disposition letter on file as a fail, since the approval is the only proof the rate may be used.
testing.done: every sampled closed filing has a SERFF disposition traced to the tracker, the notification and the stored letter.

testing.step: Test the handling of overdue and deemed filings
actions: List sampled filings that passed their decision-due date without a disposition and read the enquiry sent through SERFF Note to Reviewer.
Where deemer approval was relied on, re-read the state's deemer provision and confirm the conditions - complete filing, no objection outstanding, full review period elapsed - were genuinely met.
Confirm a written counsel opinion pre-dates any use of a deemed rate.
Record any rate used on an assumed deemer without a counsel opinion as a reportable breach.
testing.done: every deemer reliance in the sample is supported by a re-read statutory provision and a pre-dated counsel opinion.

testing.step: Log every submission and disposition exception
actions: Raise one issue per exception with company, state, SERFF tracking number, exception category and premium exposure.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: late package handover, wrong filing type, fee not paid, tracker not updated, status sweep missed, disposition not captured.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and require a control change where the same root cause appears in more than two filings.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the submission test
actions: Compute the late-submission rate and the missing-disposition rate against the stated zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the timeliness recomputation and disposition tracing evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who submitted none of the sampled filings, sign the workpaper.
File the signed workpaper under REG-002 and report late submissions and disapprovals to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rates and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - the pre-use restriction and the deemer conditions are read from each state's rating law at gate-setting time, with the Alabama prior-approval and file-and-use provisions administered by ALDOI as the representative source and California, Arizona and Connecticut checked for the same release

In-scope processes.value: Rate release gating: per-state earliest-use dating of rate tables, quote and bind blocking for ungated states, renewal offer suppression, and release of the gate only against a recorded disposition or deemer

In-scope systems.value: Rate tables are effective-dated per state in policy administration and the quote path is blocked for any state without a recorded approval; the filing tracker holds the authoritative approval date

Compliance procedure documented.value: Rate Pre-Use Gate Procedure - gate creation at determination, per-state earliest-use dating, deemer verification rules, quote/bind block configuration, gate release authority and post-release verification

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Product Officer and the Head of Compliance; the gate-release authority list is re-approved every six months

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing / pre-use gate - the tracked date is each state's approved new-business and renewal effective date; the gate cannot open earlier even by one day, and renewal offers must be dated from the approved renewal date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Alerts to the Insurance Product Manager and the rating configuration owner at approval-received, at approved-effective-date minus 10 days, and on any attempt to release a gate without a recorded disposition

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The gate record per state - blocked-from date, approval or deemer basis, releasing person, release timestamp and the disposition letter relied on - retained 7 years from rate withdrawal

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any quote, new business policy or renewal rated on an unapproved rate is logged as a use-before-approval breach with the policy count, premium involved, refund assessment and self-report decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off any early gate release, and jointly with Regulatory Counsel signs the remediation plan - rerate, refund, endorsement - for any use-before-approval breach

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All new business and renewal policies with an effective date in the quarter whose premium was calculated using a rate version filed under REG-002, by state and writing company

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - one policy rated on a rate version before its approved effective date is a fail, triggers a refund exposure assessment and escalates to the Chief Product Officer and Regulatory Counsel within 2 business days

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation bites at every rate release; the gate is tested at each release go-live and re-tested quarterly across all policies bound in the quarter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Product Operations and must not hold gate-release authority

Evidence location for test results.value: Release gate test workpaper - bound policy extract, rate version mapping, approval date join, exception list with premium - in the compliance evidence repository under REG-002

Regulator-ready documentation.value: A per-state schedule of rate version, approved effective date and first policy bound on that version, producible for a department market conduct rate review within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Counsel decides and drafts any self-report of use before approval; the Regulatory Affairs Manager delivers it to the department and owns follow-up correspondence

checklist.step: Create the per-state release gate from the determination log
actions: Take every determination row marked PRIOR APPROVAL or FILE-AND-USE and create a gate record for that state, company and rate version.
Set each gate to Blocked with the reason Pending state disposition and the SERFF tracking number recorded on it.
Set the gate's provisional earliest-use date to the state's requested effective date, marked provisional until a disposition arrives.
Publish the gate list to Pricing, Underwriting and the rating configuration owner so nobody plans a single national go-live.
checklist.done: every filing-required state has a Blocked gate record naming the rate version, SERFF tracking number and provisional earliest-use date.

checklist.step: Effective-date the rate tables per state rather than per release
actions: Load the new rate version into policy administration with a state-specific effective date taken from the gate record, not a single release-wide date.
Leave the effective date null or set to a far-future placeholder for any state whose gate is still Blocked, so the version cannot be selected by the rating engine.
Confirm the rating engine selects the rate version by risk state and effective date, and record the selection rule in the change record.
Screenshot the loaded effective dates per state and attach them to the change record.
checklist.done: each state's rate version carries its own effective date and no blocked state has a usable effective date loaded.

checklist.step: Block the quote and bind path for ungated states
actions: Configure the quote path so a submission in a Blocked state cannot select the new rate version and falls back to the currently approved version.
Configure a hard stop that prevents binding new business on a rate version whose gate is Blocked, with a message naming the state and the SERFF tracking number.
Suppress renewal offers generated on the new rate version for blocked states so renewal notices do not go out on unapproved rates.
Test the block in the pre-production environment for one blocked state and one open state and record both results.
checklist.done: quote, bind and renewal-offer paths are blocked for every state whose gate is Blocked, with the block proven in a test.

checklist.step: Verify the approval before touching the gate
actions: Open the SERFF filing named on the gate record and read the Disposition tab rather than relying on an email saying it was approved.
Confirm the disposition status is Approved, Filed or Acknowledged as that state's rating law requires for use.
Record the approved new-business effective date and the approved renewal effective date exactly as the state stated them.
Attach the disposition letter to the gate record before any release action is possible.
checklist.done: the gate record carries a downloaded disposition letter and the approved new-business and renewal dates read from SERFF.

checklist.step: Verify a deemer before relying on it
actions: Where no explicit approval exists, re-read the state's deemer provision and list its conditions: a complete filing, the full review period elapsed from the submission date, and no objection outstanding.
Check the SERFF correspondence for any objection that suspended or restarted the clock and recompute the elapsed period accordingly.
Issue a written deemer opinion naming the statute, the submission date, the computed deemer date and the conclusion.
Attach the opinion to the gate record; no deemer may be relied on without it.
checklist.done: every deemer reliance carries a written counsel opinion with the statute, the submission date and the computed deemer date.

checklist.step: Set the approved earliest-use dates on the gate
actions: Replace the provisional earliest-use date with the state's approved new-business effective date and approved renewal effective date.
Where the state approved a later date than requested, change the release plan to the approved date rather than negotiating internally around it.
Where the state approved the filing in part, record which elements are usable and which are excluded on the gate record.
Notify Pricing and Underwriting of every state whose approved dates differ from the plan.
checklist.done: every gate shows the state's approved dates and any partial approval is itemised on the record.

checklist.step: Release the gate under named authority
actions: Confirm the gate record holds a disposition letter or a counsel deemer opinion, and the approved effective dates.
Release the gate only if the current date is on or after the approved new-business effective date, or schedule the release to open automatically on that date.
Record the releasing person, the release timestamp and the evidence relied on; releases are restricted to the approved authority list.
Reject any release request that arrives with an email approval and no disposition document.
checklist.done: the gate is released only against a stored disposition or deemer opinion, on or after the approved date, with the releaser recorded.

checklist.step: Update the rating configuration to the approved effective dates
actions: Set the rate version effective date in the rating platform to the approved new-business date for that state, and the renewal date where the state gave a different one.
