Where the approval reduced or excluded elements, load only the approved factors and remove the excluded ones from the state's version.
Run a regression quote set for that state on the day before and the day of the approved date and confirm the version switches on the right day.
Attach the regression output to the change record.
checklist.done: the rating platform switches to the approved version exactly on the approved date, proven by a dated regression quote set.

checklist.step: Hold renewal offers to the approved renewal effective date
actions: Identify the renewal lead time used in that state (commonly 45 to 60 days of advance notice) and work out which renewal batch would first quote the new rates.
Confirm the renewal batch dating means no renewal notice on the new rates leaves before the approved renewal effective date.
Where the approval arrived too late for the planned batch, hold the renewals on the currently approved rates and record the decision.
Sample five renewal notices from the first affected batch and confirm the rate version printed matches the approved one.
checklist.done: no renewal notice on the new rates is issued for a policy whose renewal effective date precedes the state's approved renewal date.

checklist.step: Keep the currently approved version live for blocked states
actions: Confirm the previously approved rate version stays selectable in every blocked state with no end date set.
Test one quote per blocked state and confirm the premium computes on the previously approved version without error.
Confirm no manual override in the underwriting workstation can pick a blocked version, and remove the override right if it can.
Record the test results per blocked state in the change record.
checklist.done: every blocked state quotes successfully on its previously approved rate version and no override can reach a blocked version.

checklist.step: Run the go-live day verification for each opening state
actions: On the approved effective date, run a scripted quote in that state and confirm the premium computes on the newly approved rate version.
Run a second quote dated the day before and confirm it computes on the previous version, proving the boundary holds in both directions.
Compare both premiums to the expected values supplied by Pricing and record any variance over 0.5%.
Record pass or fail per state and hold the state closed if the boundary test fails.
checklist.done: each opening state has a same-day boundary test proving the correct version applies on and before the approved date.

checklist.step: Monitor for policies bound on a version before its approved date
actions: Run a daily report joining bound policies to the rate version used and to the gate record's approved effective date for that state.
Flag any policy whose bind or effective date precedes the approved date for its rate version.
Raise a breach the same day it appears rather than waiting for the quarterly test, since each further day adds refund exposure.
Circulate the daily zero-breach confirmation to the Insurance Product Manager.
checklist.done: a daily use-before-approval report runs, and any hit is raised as a breach on the day it appears.

checklist.step: Remediate any use before approval
actions: Quantify the affected policies, the premium charged on the unapproved version and the difference against the approved version.

Decide the remediation with the Chief Product Officer: rerate and refund the difference, endorse the policies to the approved rate, or leave in place where the charge was lower and the state permits it.
Decide whether the state requires a self-report and, where it does, draft the notification for delivery by the Regulatory Affairs Manager.
Record the decision, the customer remediation dates and the refund total on the breach issue.
checklist.done: every use-before-approval breach has a quantified exposure, a customer remediation decision and a documented self-report decision.

checklist.step: Close the gate record once the state is live and verified
actions: Confirm the gate holds disposition evidence, approved dates, the release record, the boundary test result and the first-policy-bound date.
Compare the first policy bound on the new version against the approved effective date and record the gap in days.
Set the gate to Closed - verified only when every field is populated.
Report any state still Blocked at release close to the Head of Compliance with the reason.
checklist.done: each gate is closed only with disposition, release record, boundary test and first-bound-policy date all present.

checklist.step: Archive the gate evidence for the retention period
actions: File the gate records, disposition letters, deemer opinions, boundary test outputs and daily monitoring confirmations under REG-002 by state and rate version.
Apply the 7-year-from-rate-withdrawal retention label.
Index by state, rate version, approved effective date and SERFF tracking number.
Confirm Internal Audit has independent read access to the gate archive.
checklist.done: gate evidence is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by state and rate version without going through Product Operations.

testing.step: Build the population of policies rated on filed rate versions
actions: Extract every new business and renewal policy with an effective date in the quarter, with risk state, writing company, rate version used, quote date, bind date and written premium.
Restrict the extract to rate versions that were filed under REG-002 during or before the quarter.
Reconcile the policy count and written premium to the production statistics for the quarter and resolve differences before sampling.
Sign the population as complete and record the extract query.
testing.done: a premium-reconciled policy population exists at rate-version level, signed as complete.

testing.step: Join every policy to the approved effective date for its rate version
actions: Join the policy population to the gate records on state, writing company and rate version.
List any policy whose rate version has no gate record - an unfiled version in use is the most serious finding available here.
Compute for every policy the days between its effective date and the approved effective date of the version used.
Isolate all rows with a negative gap as candidate use-before-approval breaches.
testing.done: every policy is joined to an approved effective date and all negative gaps are isolated as breach candidates.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of states and policies
actions: Take 100% of breach candidates and 100% of prior-approval states in the release.
Take 20 policies by seeded random selection from the remaining population, spread across at least five states.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date.
Include at least three renewal policies, since renewal dating is where the gate most often leaks.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all breach candidates, all prior-approval states and a random remainder is documented.

testing.step: Verify the approval evidence behind each sampled state gate
actions: Open the SERFF filing for each sampled state and read the disposition status and approved effective dates directly.
Compare them to the dates recorded on the gate record and to the dates loaded in policy administration.
Confirm the stored disposition letter is the same document SERFF holds.
Treat a gate released on an email approval with no disposition document as a control failure.
testing.done: every sampled gate's approved dates are independently confirmed in SERFF and agree with the gate record and the system dates.

testing.step: Re-perform the deemer computation where deemer was relied on
actions: For each sampled gate opened on deemer, recompute the deemer date as submission date plus the statutory review period, adjusted for any objection suspension shown in the SERFF correspondence.
Confirm no objection was outstanding at the recomputed deemer date and that the filing was complete when submitted.
Compare the recomputed deemer date to the date the gate was actually released.
Record any gate opened before its recomputed deemer date as a reportable breach.
testing.done: every deemer-based gate release is recomputed and shown to fall on or after the statutory deemer date.

testing.step: Re-perform the rating boundary test in the live system
actions: For each sampled state, run a quote dated the approved effective date and a quote dated the day before, using identical risk characteristics.
Confirm the two quotes use different rate versions and that the earlier date uses the previously approved version.
Compare each premium to the expected figure supplied independently by Pricing and record variances.
Capture both quote outputs with their rate version identifiers into the workpaper.
testing.done: the version boundary is independently proven in the live system for every sampled state, with both quote outputs captured.

testing.step: Test renewal offer dating against the approved renewal date
actions: For each sampled renewal, read the renewal notice issue date, the policy renewal effective date and the rate version printed on the notice.
Compare the renewal effective date to the state's approved renewal effective date recorded on the gate.
Confirm no notice quoting the new rates was issued for a renewal effective before the approved renewal date.
Trace one notice end to end from the batch record to the customer document image.
testing.done: no sampled renewal notice quoted new rates ahead of the state's approved renewal effective date, with one traced end to end.

testing.step: Quantify the exposure on every confirmed breach
actions: For each confirmed use-before-approval policy, recompute the premium on the previously approved version and take the difference.
Total the overcharge and undercharge separately by state, since only the overcharge usually drives refunds.
Count affected policyholders per state, because the state's interest scales with policyholder count.
Present the exposure schedule to Regulatory Counsel within 2 business days of confirmation.
testing.done: every confirmed breach has a recomputed premium difference, a per-state overcharge total and a policyholder count delivered to counsel.

testing.step: Log every gate exception with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception with state, rate version, policy count, premium exposure and the gate record involved.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: gate released without disposition, national effective date used, deemer miscomputed, renewal batch dating, override right left open, monitoring report not run.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel for every overcharge breach.
Carry every open exception into the next release's gate test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where premium was overcharged, a self-report assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the gate test
actions: Report the number of policies rated before approval against the zero-tolerance threshold, with premium and policyholder counts by state.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the boundary tests and the approval verification evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who holds no gate-release authority, sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper under REG-002 and report every breach and its remediation status to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, breach counts with premium, and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: IT and Product jointly own implementation; the Policy Admin Ops Lead is accountable that the rates coded in policy administration and the rating engine are byte-for-byte the rates the state approved

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - the approved rate pages and disposition letter from the state filing are the controlling text for implementation, not the internal pricing model; the Alabama filing approved by ALDOI is the representative source and each state's own approved pages control that state

In-scope processes.value: Rate implementation: rate table and factor loading, rating algorithm changes, tier and territory table updates, manual rule coding, quote/issue/renewal regression testing, and production release of the approved rate version per state

In-scope systems.value: Rate factors and algorithm steps are configured in the rating platform and consumed by policy administration; changes travel through the ITSM change record with the SERFF tracking number attached

Compliance procedure documented.value: Approved Rate Implementation Procedure - approved-pages handover, configuration build from approved pages only, independent factor-level reconciliation, regression and boundary testing, change approval, production release and post-release verification

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of IT and the Chief Actuary; re-approved annually and whenever the rating engine or policy administration release process changes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing - configuration must be complete, reconciled and regression-tested before the state's approved new-business effective date, with the code release scheduled no later than 5 business days ahead of that date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Change-record milestones at approval-received, configuration-complete, reconciliation-signed, regression-passed and release-scheduled, each dated back from the approved effective date, with escalation at approved date minus 5 days if regression has not passed

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Approved rate pages used as the build source, the factor-level reconciliation sign-off, regression and boundary test results, the change record and the release log, retained 7 years from rate withdrawal

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any coded factor that differs from the approved rate page, any algorithm step not in the approved filing, and any release made without a signed reconciliation is logged as an exception with premium impact and correction date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off any correction to a mis-coded approved rate, including the rerate and refund population, before the fix is released

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every approved rate version implemented in the quarter, at factor level, plus a sample of policies rated on each version, by state and writing company

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero variance at factor level - any coded factor differing from the approved page is a fail regardless of premium effect; policy-level premium re-performance must match to the cent, with any difference investigated to root cause

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is per filing; implementation is tested at every release before go-live and re-tested quarterly on bound policies across all versions implemented in the quarter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: The factor-level reconciliation must be performed by an actuary who did not configure the rating platform and did not build the filing exhibits

Evidence location for test results.value: Implementation accuracy workpaper - approved page to configuration reconciliation, regression pack, policy-level premium re-performance, exception list - in the compliance evidence repository under REG-002

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The approved rate pages alongside a system extract of the coded factors and a worked premium calculation for a named policy, producible for a department rate examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Affairs Manager fields any department question about rates charged; the Policy Admin Ops Lead supplies the system extract and worked calculation, and Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of a mis-coded rate

checklist.step: Take handover of the approved rate pages as the only build source
actions: Collect from the Regulatory Filing Specialist the approval notice, the disposition letter and the approved rate pages as downloaded from the SERFF filing.
Confirm the approved pages carry the state, company, edition date and the SERFF tracking number, and refuse any pack that is a pricing working file instead.
Record on the change record which document version is the build source and lock it read-only.
Reject any late change to the source pages that has not itself been filed and approved.
checklist.done: the build source is the approved SERFF rate pages, locked read-only and named on the change record.

checklist.step: Raise the change record and tie it to the filing
actions: Open a normal change record for the rate implementation naming the state, writing company, rate version and SERFF tracking number in the title.
Attach the approved rate pages, the disposition letter and the gate record showing the approved effective date.
Set the implementation window at least 5 business days before the approved new-business effective date so a failed release can be retried.
Name the configuration builder, the independent reconciler and the release approver on the record - all three must be different people.
checklist.done: a change record exists carrying the SERFF tracking number, approved pages, approved effective date and three separate named roles.

checklist.step: Load base rates, factors and relativities from the approved pages
actions: Build the new rate version in the rating platform from the approved pages, entering base rates, factor tables and relativities exactly as printed including decimal places and rounding.
Set the version effective date to the state's approved new-business effective date and the renewal date where the state approved a different one.
Do not carry forward any factor from the countrywide template that is not on this state's approved pages.
Export the loaded factor tables to a reconciliation file for the independent reviewer.
checklist.done: the state's rate version is loaded from the approved pages only, effective-dated correctly, with a factor export ready for reconciliation.

checklist.step: Implement territory and tier definition changes
actions: Load the approved territory definition - the ZIP, county or rating territory mapping exactly as filed - into the reference data service the rating engine reads.
Load the approved tier definitions with their qualifying criteria and tier factors, keeping the tier variable names used in the filing.
Confirm every ZIP or county in the state maps to exactly one territory and that no code is left unmapped, since an unmapped code defaults silently.
Produce a mapping count by territory and compare it to the exposure counts in the filing exhibits.
checklist.done: territory and tier tables match the approved definitions with no unmapped codes, and mapping counts tie to the filing exhibits.

checklist.step: Implement rating algorithm and rating rule changes
actions: Code the algorithm steps in the order the approved manual pages set out, including the order of multiplication, any capping step and the rounding rule at each step.
Implement the approved rating rules - eligibility, minimum premium, maximum discount stacking - as filed, and nothing that was not filed.
Where the approval excluded or modified an element, remove it from the build rather than leaving it disabled by a flag someone can turn on.
Peer review the code change against the approved pages and record the reviewer on the pull request.
checklist.done: the algorithm, rounding and rules match the approved manual pages step for step, with a recorded peer review.

checklist.step: Reconcile every coded factor back to the approved page independently
actions: Take the factor export from the rating platform and the approved rate pages and compare them cell by cell for every table.
Reconcile counts first - number of factor rows per table - then values, and flag any factor present in one source and not the other.
Check decimal precision and rounding, since a factor truncated at four places instead of five is still a mis-coded rate.
Sign the reconciliation naming the approved page version and the rating platform version compared, and return every difference to the Configuration Engineer for correction and re-reconciliation.
Refuse to sign a partial reconciliation.
checklist.done: a signed, zero-difference factor-level reconciliation exists between the approved pages and the loaded configuration.

checklist.step: Build the regression quote pack from the filing exhibits
actions: Ask Pricing for expected premiums on at least 25 test risks per state covering each territory band, each tier, minimum premium cases and the largest and smallest discount stacks.
Run each risk through the new rate version and compare the system premium to the expected premium to the cent.
Investigate every difference to a specific algorithm step rather than accepting a tolerance.
Store the regression pack with inputs, expected values, actual values and the rate version identifier.
checklist.done: a 25-risk-per-state regression pack runs with every premium matching the Pricing expectation to the cent, or each difference explained.

checklist.step: Test the disruption outcome against what was filed
actions: Rerate the in-force book for the state on the newly coded version and compute the actual statewide rate level impact and the disruption distribution.
Compare both to the figures certified in the actuarial memorandum and filed on the SERFF Rate Information tab.
Investigate any difference above 0.5 percentage points, since it means either the filing or the implementation is wrong and both are reportable.
Record the comparison and sign it before release approval.
checklist.done: the rerated statewide impact and disruption reproduce the certified filing figures within 0.5 points, with any gap investigated.

checklist.step: Test the effective-date boundary in both directions
actions: Quote an identical risk dated the day before the approved effective date and on the approved date and confirm the rate version switches exactly on the boundary.
Repeat for a renewal transaction using the approved renewal effective date.
Confirm a mid-term endorsement on a policy written before the approved date still rates on the version in force at inception, as the filing states.
Capture the version identifier returned by each quote into the test evidence.
checklist.done: new business, renewal and endorsement transactions each select the correct rate version across the approved-date boundary.

checklist.step: Test downstream premium display and documents
actions: Issue a test policy on the new version and confirm the premium flows correctly to billing, the installment schedule and the commission calculation.
Confirm the declarations page and the rating information notice print the correct premium, manual edition and any state-required rate change disclosure.
Confirm agent-facing quote screens in the broker portal show the same premium as the policy system.
Log defects against the change record and block release on any premium mismatch between systems.
checklist.done: premium, documents, billing and commission all reflect the same approved-version premium on a test policy.

checklist.step: Approve the release with the compliance evidence attached
actions: Confirm the change record holds the approved pages, the signed factor reconciliation, the regression pack, the disruption comparison and the boundary test results.
Confirm the gate record for the state shows an approval or a counsel deemer opinion.
Obtain approval from the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Compliance Analyst, and refuse the release if the reconciliation sign-off is missing.
Schedule the release inside the approved window and record the approver names and timestamps.
checklist.done: the release is approved only with reconciliation, regression, disruption and gate evidence attached, and the approvers are recorded.

checklist.step: Release to production and verify the same day
actions: Deploy the rate version and reference data through the standard pipeline and record the deployment identifier on the change record.
Immediately after deployment, run three smoke quotes in production for the state and compare their premiums to the regression expectations.
Confirm in the production configuration screen that the version effective date reads the approved date, not the deployment date.
Roll back and re-plan if any smoke quote disagrees, rather than correcting live.
checklist.done: the version is deployed, the production effective date reads the approved date, and three production smoke quotes match expectations.

checklist.step: Verify the first live policies on the new version
actions: On the first two business days after the approved effective date, extract the first 20 policies bound in that state on the new version.
Recompute the premium for five of them by hand from the approved rate pages and compare to the charged premium.
Confirm none has an effective date earlier than the approved date.
Report the result to the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Insurance Product Manager and raise a breach on any difference.
checklist.done: five live policies are hand-recomputed from the approved pages and agree with the premium charged.

checklist.step: Correct any mis-coded rate and remediate affected policies
actions: Where a coded factor differs from the approved page, stop new business on the affected version in that state the same day.
Quantify the affected policy population and the premium difference against the approved rates.
Approve the correction, the rerate population and the refund or endorsement approach, and set the customer remediation dates.
Ask Regulatory Counsel to decide whether the state requires notification of a mis-charged approved rate.
checklist.done: every mis-coded factor is corrected, the affected population quantified and remediated, and the notification decision recorded.

checklist.step: Archive the implementation evidence
actions: File the approved pages, factor reconciliation, regression pack, disruption comparison, boundary tests, change record and deployment log under REG-002 by state and rate version.
Apply the 7-year-from-rate-withdrawal retention label.
Index by state, rate version, SERFF tracking number and approved effective date so a department question about a specific policy can be answered from the archive.
Confirm Internal Audit has read access without needing IT to retrieve the records.
checklist.done: implementation evidence is archived, retention-labelled and independently retrievable by state and rate version.

testing.step: Build the population of rate versions implemented in the quarter
actions: Extract every change record deploying a rate version in the quarter with state, company, rate version, SERFF tracking number and deployment date.
Reconcile the change records to the rating platform version history so a configuration change made outside the change process is exposed.
Add versions deployed as emergency changes, since those are where reconciliation is most often skipped.
Sign the population as complete and record both extract sources.
testing.done: a change-record-to-rating-platform reconciled population of implemented versions exists, signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every implemented version to an approved filing
actions: Match each implemented version to a SERFF filing with an Approved or Filed disposition for that state and company.
List versions implemented with no matching approved filing as automatic exceptions.
Confirm the version effective date in the rating platform equals the approved effective date on the disposition.
Quantify written premium earned on any unmatched version.
testing.done: every implemented version ties to an approved filing with matching effective dates, or is listed as an exception with premium.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of versions and policies
actions: Take 100% of versions implemented under emergency change and 100% of versions in prior-approval states.
Take 8 further versions by seeded random selection, then draw 5 bound policies per selected version by seeded random selection.
Record the seed, the population sizes at both levels and the selection date.
Confirm the policy sample includes new business, renewal and at least two endorsements.
testing.done: a two-stage reproducible sample of versions and policies is documented, covering emergency and prior-approval versions in full.

testing.step: Re-perform the factor-level reconciliation independently
actions: Download the approved rate pages from the SERFF filing rather than from the internal folder, so the comparison uses the regulator's copy.
Extract the loaded factor tables from the rating platform for the sampled versions and compare cell by cell.
Compare row counts per table first, then values, then decimal precision.
Record every difference with table name, key, approved value and coded value - no tolerance applies.
testing.done: every sampled version is reconciled against the SERFF copy of the approved pages with all differences listed.

testing.step: Re-perform policy premiums by hand from the approved pages
actions: For each sampled policy, take the rating characteristics from the policy record and compute the premium manually following the approved manual page algorithm.
Apply the approved rounding at each step in the order the manual sets out, since rounding order alone can move the answer.
Compare to the premium charged and reconcile any difference to a specific algorithm step or factor.
Record the full worked calculation in the workpaper - this is the exhibit a department examiner will ask for.
testing.done: each sampled policy has a full hand-worked premium from the approved pages that agrees with the premium charged.

testing.step: Verify territory and tier mapping integrity
actions: Extract the territory mapping in force for each sampled state and confirm every ZIP or county code maps to exactly one filed territory.
Compare the mapping to the territory definition filed with the state, and list codes present in one and not the other.
For sampled policies, confirm the territory the policy was rated in matches the mapping for its risk address.
Flag any policy rated on a default territory as a mis-rating exception.
testing.done: territory and tier mappings match the filed definitions with no unmapped or defaulted codes in the sample.

testing.step: Verify the change control evidence behind each sampled release
actions: Open each sampled change record and confirm it holds the approved rate pages, the signed factor reconciliation, the regression pack and the boundary test results.
Confirm the builder, the reconciler and the release approver are three different people.
Confirm the release approval timestamp pre-dates the deployment timestamp.
List releases deployed without a signed reconciliation as control failures regardless of whether the rates turned out correct.
testing.done: every sampled release has complete, pre-dated change evidence with segregation of builder, reconciler and approver proven.

testing.step: Recompute the realised rate level impact against the certified figure
actions: For each sampled state, compute the realised average premium change on renewals rated on the new version against their prior-term premium at prior rates.
Compare the realised impact to the statewide rate level change certified to the department in the filing.
Investigate any gap above 1 percentage point and attribute it to mix, exposure change or implementation error.
Record implementation-driven gaps as exceptions, since they mean policyholders were not charged the filed rates.
testing.done: the realised rate level change is compared to the certified figure for every sampled state and any implementation-driven gap is raised.

testing.step: Log every implementation exception with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception with state, rate version, factor or step involved, affected policy count and premium difference.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: built from a working file, factor mistyped, rounding order wrong, unmapped territory code, unfiled element left enabled, reconciliation skipped.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and require rerate and refund where policyholders were overcharged against the approved rates.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where overcharged, a rerate and refund commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the implementation test
actions: Report the factor-level variance count against the zero-variance threshold and the policy-level premium re-performance results.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the reconciliation and hand-worked premium evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither configured nor reconciled the sampled versions, sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper under REG-002 and report mis-coded rates and their remediation to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, factor variance count and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the objection response end to end - receipt, routing, drafting, clearance and submission inside SERFF - with the Product / Filing Actuary owning the actuarial content of the answer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - the response deadline is taken from the objection letter itself and from the state's SERFF filing rules for objection response times, re-read on receipt; Alabama, Arizona, California and Connecticut each set their own response windows and none is assumed from another state

In-scope processes.value: Objection and interrogatory handling on open rate filings: receipt and logging, deadline computation, routing to actuarial or legal, drafting and clearing the response, amending exhibits or rates, and submitting the response inside the SERFF filing

In-scope systems.value: Objections arrive on the SERFF Objection Letters tab and responses are submitted through Respond to Objection; each objection is mirrored into the internal objection log the same business day

Compliance procedure documented.value: Rate Filing Objection Response Procedure - daily objection sweep, deadline computation from the letter, routing matrix by objection type, drafting and actuarial or legal clearance, extension requests, and response submission with evidence capture

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Actuary; reviewed annually and after any state changes its stated objection response window

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven - the clock starts on the objection letter date and runs for the period the letter states (commonly 10, 15 or 30 days); the internal target is to respond by day 7 of the stated window, and an extension must be requested before the deadline, never after

Deadline reminders configured.value: Objection log alerts on receipt day, at deadline minus 5 business days and at deadline minus 2 business days, escalating to the Regulatory Affairs Manager at minus 2 if no draft response exists

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The objection letter, the internal routing record, drafts, the actuarial or legal clearance, the submitted response with its attachments and the state's acknowledgement, retained 7 years from rate withdrawal

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Objections answered after the stated deadline, objections answered without the required clearance, and filings disapproved or closed for non-response are each logged with root cause and the effect on the target effective date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late response, every extension request and every decision to amend the filed rate in answer to an objection

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All objection letters and interrogatories received on rate filings during the quarter, plus objections open at quarter start, taken from the SERFF Objection Letters tab across every company instance

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero late responses - any response submitted after the deadline stated in the objection letter without a granted extension is a fail; any filing closed or disapproved for non-response escalates immediately to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is event-driven, so the objection log is swept daily in operation and tested quarterly across every objection received in the quarter, at 100% for objections that changed a filed rate

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted or submitted any sampled objection response

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly objection response workpaper - SERFF objection extract, deadline recomputation, response tracing, clearance inspection, exception list - in the compliance evidence repository under REG-002

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The complete objection thread from the SERFF filing - letter, response, attachments and acknowledgement - with the internal clearance record, producible per filing within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: All responses go back to the examiner inside the SERFF filing and never by side email; Regulatory Counsel clears any response that concedes an error and the Chief Actuary clears any response that changes a certified figure

checklist.step: Sweep SERFF for new objections every business day
actions: Each business morning open the SERFF filing list for every company instance and filter to status Pending Industry Response.
Open each filing's Objection Letters tab and download any letter not already logged.
Confirm the SERFF email notifications route to a monitored shared mailbox as well as the named filing contact, so an absence does not lose a deadline.
Record the sweep completion each day, including nil returns, so a missed sweep is visible.
checklist.done: the daily sweep is recorded for every company instance and every new objection letter is downloaded the day it appears.

checklist.step: Log the objection and compute its response deadline
actions: Create an objection log entry with SERFF tracking number, state, company, objection letter date, examiner name and the number of questions raised.
Read the response period from the letter itself, and where the letter is silent use the period stated in the state's SERFF filing rules; record which source you used.
Compute the response deadline from the letter date, noting whether the state counts calendar or business days, and set the internal target at day 7 of the window.
Record whether the state's review clock is suspended while the objection is open, because that moves the deemer date too.
Set alerts at deadline minus 5 and minus 2 business days.
checklist.done: the objection is logged with a computed deadline, the source of the response period, the clock-suspension effect and alerts set.

checklist.step: Split the objection into individually answerable questions
actions: Break the letter into numbered questions, keeping the examiner's own numbering so the response maps one to one.
Classify each question as actuarial support, rating rule or manual language, form or disclosure, data or exhibit, or legal interpretation.
Assign an owner per question from the routing matrix and give each a due date at least 3 business days before the response deadline.
Flag any question that implies the state will require a rate change, since that needs Pricing and the Chief Actuary immediately.
checklist.done: every numbered question has a classification, a named owner and a due date ahead of the response deadline.

checklist.step: Route actuarial questions and gather the support
actions: Take each actuarial question and identify the exhibit or selection it targets - trend, development, expense provision, credibility, profit or the complement of credibility.
Rebuild the supporting analysis at the level of detail the examiner asked for, for example experience by accident year, by coverage or by territory.
Where the examiner challenges a selection, prepare the alternative the examiner implies and quantify what it does to the indicated change, so the decision is informed rather than defended blind.
Send the analysis to the Regulatory Filing Specialist with the exhibit numbering the response will use.
checklist.done: each actuarial question has rebuilt support at the requested granularity and a quantified alternative where a selection is challenged.

checklist.step: Route rating rule and manual language questions
actions: Take each rule or manual question and locate the exact manual page and paragraph the examiner is reading.
Prepare either an explanation of how the rule operates with a worked example, or a revised manual page if the examiner's reading shows the language is genuinely unclear.
Where a revision is needed, produce a redline against the submitted page, not against the previously approved page.
Confirm with Underwriting that any revised rule can actually be operated as written before offering it to the state.
checklist.done: each rule question has a worked explanation or a redlined revision that Underwriting has confirmed is operable.

checklist.step: Route legal and prohibited-factor questions to counsel
actions: Take questions challenging the permissibility of a rating variable, the certification wording or the statutory basis of the filing.
Re-read the state's rating law and any bulletin the examiner cites, and draft the legal position with the citation quoted.
Advise whether to defend the variable, restrict it in that state, or withdraw it from the filing, and state the risk of each route.
Clear the wording of any response sentence that could read as an admission of an unfiled or impermissible rate.
checklist.done: every legal question has a drafted position with quoted authority and a stated recommendation on defend, restrict or withdraw.

checklist.step: Decide whether to amend the filed rate in response
actions: Where the examiner requires a lower rate or a changed selection, convene Pricing, Product and Regulatory Counsel within 2 business days.
Quantify the revised indicated change, the revised statewide rate level impact and the effect on the state's expected loss ratio.
Decide in writing between accepting the examiner's position, offering a compromise with support, or withdrawing the filing in that state.
Where a figure certified in the memorandum changes, prepare a revised certification page rather than silently amending an exhibit.
checklist.done: any rate amendment has a dated written decision, a recomputed statewide impact and, where certified figures move, a revised certification.

checklist.step: Draft the consolidated response
actions: Draft the response repeating each of the examiner's numbered questions verbatim, followed by the answer and the attachment reference that supports it.
Answer every question, including those where the answer is that no change is being made, and never leave a question unaddressed.
Keep the tone factual and avoid arguing the state's law back at the examiner; state the support and the citation.
Name the attachments so the examiner can see which question each belongs to, for example Objection-1-Q3-trend-by-accident-year.pdf.
checklist.done: a drafted response answers every numbered question in the examiner's own order with named supporting attachments.

checklist.step: Clear the response before it is submitted
actions: Route the draft to the Product / Filing Actuary for actuarial accuracy and to Regulatory Counsel for any legal or admission content.
Where any certified figure changed, require the Chief Actuary's sign-off on the revised figure and the revised certification page.
Check the response does not contradict anything already stated in the filing or in a response to another state.
Record each clearance with name and date on the objection log entry.
checklist.done: the response carries dated actuarial and legal clearances and, where figures changed, a Chief Actuary sign-off before submission.

checklist.step: Request an extension before the deadline where one is needed
actions: Where the analysis genuinely cannot be completed in the window, send the extension request through the SERFF filing at least 3 business days before the deadline.
State the reason, the specific questions needing more time and the date you will respond by.
Record the request, the examiner's answer and the revised deadline on the objection log; an ungranted request does not move the deadline.
Never let a deadline pass on the assumption that an extension will be granted.
checklist.done: every extension is requested inside SERFF before the deadline, with the reason, proposed date and the examiner's answer logged.

checklist.step: Submit the response inside the SERFF filing
actions: Open the objection on the Objection Letters tab and use Respond to Objection so the response attaches to the correct letter.
Satisfy each objected item on the Rate/Rule or Supporting Documentation schedule, replacing amended exhibits rather than adding a second version of the same exhibit.
Attach the response document and all supporting attachments, then submit and capture the confirmation screen with its date and time.
Update the objection log with the response date, the days used against the deadline and the new filing status.
checklist.done: the response is submitted against the correct objection letter with amended exhibits replacing superseded ones, and the confirmation is captured.

checklist.step: Re-baseline the package after any amendment
actions: Update the package baseline to the amended exhibits, memorandum and manual pages actually now on file with the state.
Mark the superseded versions clearly so implementation cannot later build from the original submission.
Notify the Policy Admin Ops Lead of any change to the rates that will eventually be implemented.
Record which baseline version corresponds to which SERFF submission date.
checklist.done: the package baseline reflects what the state now holds and superseded versions are marked so they cannot be built from.

checklist.step: Recompute the effective date impact of the objection cycle
actions: Recompute the expected disposition date allowing for the days the objection consumed and any clock suspension the state applies.
Compare it to the target rate effective date and to the implementation lead time still required.
Where the target date is no longer reachable, decide and record whether to move the effective date, drop the state from the release or launch on the previously approved rates.
Update the gate record and the release plan with the revised dates.
checklist.done: the revised disposition date is computed and the release plan and gate record reflect a reachable effective date or a recorded alternative.

checklist.step: Close the objection only when the state moves the filing on
actions: Watch the filing status after submission and confirm it leaves Pending Industry Response.
Where a further objection arrives on the same point, log it as a new objection and record it as a repeat so the root cause is visible.
Close the log entry only when the filing status has changed and the response is visible on the SERFF thread.
Record the total elapsed days from letter to closure for trend reporting.
checklist.done: each objection entry closes only after the filing status moves on, with repeat objections logged separately and elapsed days recorded.

checklist.step: Archive the objection thread with its clearances
actions: Export the full objection thread - letter, drafts, clearances, submitted response, attachments and state acknowledgement - under REG-002 by state and SERFF tracking number.
Apply the 7-year-from-rate-withdrawal retention label.
Index by examiner name, objection type and state so recurring examiner concerns can be found before the next filing.
Publish a quarterly summary of objection themes by state to the Product / Filing Actuary so future packages pre-empt them.
checklist.done: the complete objection thread is archived, retention-labelled and indexed by objection type, with a themes summary issued to the filing team.

testing.step: Build the population of objections received in the quarter
actions: Export from SERFF every objection letter dated inside the quarter across all company instances, plus objections open at quarter start.
Export the internal objection log for the same period and match on SERFF tracking number and objection letter date.
List objections present in SERFF but absent from the log - these represent deadlines nobody was tracking.
Sign the reconciled population as complete and record both export dates.
testing.done: a two-way reconciled SERFF-to-log objection population exists, with unlogged objections identified and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every objection to a submitted response
actions: Match each objection to a response submitted on the SERFF Objection Letters thread.
List objections with no response, responses submitted outside the objection thread, and filings closed or disapproved for non-response.
Confirm each response addresses every numbered question in the letter by comparing question counts.
Treat a partially answered objection as an exception, since a partial answer restarts the cycle and burns the deemer runway.
testing.done: every objection is matched to a complete response on the correct thread, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of objections
actions: Take 100% of objections that resulted in a change to a filed rate or a certified figure, and 100% of repeat objections on the same point.
Take 15 further objections by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum total of 25.
Record the seed, the population size, the stratification and the selection date.
Confirm the sample covers at least four states and both prior-approval and file-and-use jurisdictions.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all rate-changing and repeat objections plus a random remainder is documented.

testing.step: Recompute the response deadline from the objection letter
actions: For each sampled objection, read the response period from the letter itself and, where silent, from the state's SERFF filing rules as they stood on the letter date.
Recompute the deadline from the letter date using the state's calendar or business day convention.
Compare the recomputed deadline to the deadline recorded in the objection log and list any difference.
Compare the actual response submission date to your recomputed deadline and record days early or late.
testing.done: each sampled objection has an independently recomputed deadline and a recorded days-early or days-late response figure.

testing.step: Verify extension requests were made before the deadline
actions: For every sampled objection answered after the original deadline, find the extension request on the SERFF thread.
Confirm the request pre-dates the original deadline and that the examiner granted it, with the granted date recorded.
Treat a response late with no granted extension as a fail, and a request made after the deadline as a fail regardless of the answer.
Capture the extension thread into the workpaper.
testing.done: every late sampled response is supported by an extension requested before the deadline and granted on the SERFF thread.

testing.step: Inspect the clearance evidence behind each response
actions: Confirm each sampled response carries a dated actuarial clearance and, where legal content was involved, a dated counsel clearance, both pre-dating submission.
Where a certified figure changed, confirm a Chief Actuary sign-off and a revised certification page were filed with the response.
Confirm the clearer is not the same person who drafted the response.
List responses submitted without the required clearance as control failures even where the answer was correct.
testing.done: every sampled response has pre-dated clearances by someone other than the drafter, with revised certifications where figures moved.

testing.step: Trace the response content back to its supporting analysis
actions: For five sampled actuarial questions, take the figure quoted in the response and trace it to the underlying exhibit or model output.
Re-perform the arithmetic behind at least two of those figures independently.
Confirm the figure quoted to the examiner is consistent with the figure in the original filing, or that the change was explicitly disclosed.
Record any answer to the examiner that cannot be traced to a retained analysis as a fail.
testing.done: every traced response figure ties to a retained analysis, with two independently re-performed and any inconsistency disclosed or raised.

testing.step: Recompute the deemer impact of the objection cycle
actions: For each sampled objection, apply the state's clock-suspension rule and recompute the revised disposition or deemer date.
Compare to the target rate effective date recorded on the gate and confirm the release plan was updated where the date became unreachable.
Confirm no state whose deemer was suspended by an open objection had its gate opened on a deemer basis.
List any gate opened during an open objection as a reportable breach.
testing.done: revised deemer dates are recomputed for every sampled objection and no gate was opened while an objection was outstanding.

testing.step: Log every objection-handling exception
actions: Raise one issue per exception with state, SERFF tracking number, objection date, deadline, response date and the effect on the target effective date.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: objection not logged, deadline miscomputed, owner unassigned, analysis late, clearance skipped, extension requested late.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and require a routing-matrix change where the same question type is repeatedly late.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the objection test
actions: Report the late-response count against the zero-tolerance threshold, plus average days to respond and the repeat-objection rate by state.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the deadline recomputation and clearance inspection evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted none of the sampled responses, sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper under REG-002 and report late responses and any filing lost to non-response to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, late-response count and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Compliance Ops owns the rate filing archive - the filed package version, the full SERFF correspondence and the approval letter for every state - and is accountable that it can be produced on examination

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - the retention period is set to the longest of the state record-retention rules for rate filings across the 51 jurisdictions and the company schedule, re-read annually; Alabama, Arizona, California and Connecticut retention provisions are checked explicitly because their examination cycles reach furthest back

In-scope processes.value: Continuous archiving of rate filing records: filed package versions, approved rate pages, objection threads, disposition letters, deemer opinions and the determination log, indexed per state, company and SERFF tracking number

In-scope systems.value: The compliance evidence repository is the system of record for filing evidence, fed from SERFF exports and the document management repository, with retention labels applied at ingestion

Compliance procedure documented.value: Rate Filing Records Retention Procedure - what constitutes the complete filing record, ingestion at disposition, indexing keys, retention label assignment, legal hold handling, access control and destruction review

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the General Counsel; the retention schedule for rate filings is re-approved annually against state retention rules

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous - the archive must be complete within 10 business days of a filing reaching a disposition, and any examination request must be met inside the department's stated response window, typically 5 to 10 business days

Deadline reminders configured.value: Repository alerts for any filing closed in SERFF for more than 10 business days without a complete archive record, plus an annual retention review alert and a destruction-eligibility review 90 days before any record's retention expiry

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed package version, approved rate pages, transmittal, fee confirmation, every objection and response, the disposition letter, deemer opinions and the determination row, retained 7 years from withdrawal of the rate and longer where a state or a legal hold requires it

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missing disposition letters, filings with no archived package version, records destroyed inside their retention period and records under legal hold that were altered are each logged with the exposure and the recovery action

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off any gap in the filing archive, any early destruction incident and any decision that a record cannot be reconstructed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All rate filings reaching a disposition in the quarter plus a sample of filings disposed in each of the prior seven years, tested for completeness and retrievability by state and SERFF tracking number

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on the disposition letter and the filed package version - a filing missing either is a fail; retrieval must succeed inside 5 business days and any record destroyed before its retention expiry is a reportable incident

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is continuous, so completeness is tested quarterly on that quarter's dispositions and annually on an aged sample drawn across the full seven-year retention window

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Compliance Ops and must perform the retrieval test themselves rather than accepting a retrieval performed by the record owner

Evidence location for test results.value: Records completeness workpaper - disposition population, archive join, retrieval timing, retention label inspection, aged-sample results - in the compliance evidence repository under REG-002

Regulator-ready documentation.value: A complete filing pack per SERFF tracking number - filed package, correspondence, approval letter and approved rate pages - assembled and delivered for a rate or market conduct examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Affairs Manager receives the examination document request and owns delivery; the Records Manager assembles the pack and General Counsel clears any claim of privilege or any statement that a record cannot be produced

checklist.step: Define what a complete rate filing record contains
actions: Publish the record definition: determination row, filed package version, transmittal, fee confirmation, every objection letter and response, the disposition letter, approved rate pages, any deemer opinion and the implementation change record reference.
Agree the definition with Regulatory Counsel and the Regulatory Filing Specialist so nothing described as optional in practice is missing at examination.
Turn the definition into a completeness checklist the repository can enforce at ingestion.
Publish the definition to the filing team and review it whenever a state adds a required document type.
checklist.done: a published, counsel-agreed record definition exists and is enforced as an ingestion checklist.

checklist.step: Export the closed filing from SERFF at disposition
actions: Within 5 business days of a filing closing, open it in SERFF and export the complete filing including all schedule attachments, correspondence and the disposition.
Download the disposition letter separately, since it is the single document that proves the rate may be used.
Download the approved rate pages as the state holds them, not as the internal folder holds them.
Hand the export to Compliance Ops with the SERFF tracking number, state filing number and disposition date.
checklist.done: a complete SERFF export with the disposition letter and approved pages is handed over within 5 business days of closure.

checklist.step: Ingest the record and apply the index keys
actions: Ingest the export under REG-002 with index keys: state, writing company and NAIC code, TOI/Sub-TOI, SERFF tracking number, state filing number, submission date, disposition date and approved effective dates.
Run the ingestion completeness checklist and reject the record back to the filing team if any defined component is missing.
Link the record to the determination log row and to the implementation change record so the chain from determination to charged rate is navigable.
Record the ingestion date and the ingesting user.
checklist.done: the record is ingested with all index keys, passes the completeness checklist and is linked to its determination and implementation records.

checklist.step: Apply the retention label and the destruction date
actions: Apply the rate filing retention label of 7 years from withdrawal of the rate, and set the computed earliest destruction date on the record.
Where a state's own retention rule is longer than the company schedule, apply the state rule for that record and note which state drove it.
Set the record read-only so the archived version cannot be edited after ingestion.
Confirm the retention clock starts at rate withdrawal, not at filing closure, since a rate in force for a decade extends the record's life.
checklist.done: each record carries a retention label, a computed destruction date keyed to rate withdrawal, and is read-only.

checklist.step: Track the in-force status that drives the retention clock
actions: Run a quarterly extract of rate versions still in force by state and company from policy administration.
Mark the corresponding archive records as in force, so their destruction dates stay unset.
For versions withdrawn in the quarter, record the withdrawal date on the archive record and let the 7-year clock start.
Reconcile the in-force list to the archive so no record is either aged out early or held indefinitely by accident.
checklist.done: every archive record's retention clock reflects the current in-force status of its rate version, reconciled quarterly.

checklist.step: Preserve the filed and approved versions distinctly
actions: Store the as-submitted package version and the as-approved version as separate labelled artifacts, since objections frequently change the content between them.
Label every superseded version Superseded with the date it was replaced and the objection that caused it.
Confirm the as-approved version is the one linked to the implementation change record.
Prevent deletion of superseded versions - the examiner may ask what was originally filed.
checklist.done: as-submitted, superseded and as-approved versions are separately labelled and preserved, with the approved version linked to implementation.

checklist.step: Archive correspondence outside SERFF as well
actions: Collect any phone-call note, email or meeting record with a department examiner about the filing and write it into a contact memo naming the examiner, date, subject and outcome.
Ingest the contact memo into the filing record so the archive is not silent about conversations SERFF never saw.
Where a call changed the filing's direction, cross-reference the objection or amendment it produced.
Remind the filing team that substantive positions belong on the SERFF thread, and memo anything that did not get there.
checklist.done: every out-of-portal examiner contact has a dated memo ingested into the filing record and cross-referenced to what it changed.

checklist.step: Control access to the archive
actions: Grant read access to Compliance, Internal Audit, Regulatory Counsel and Product Compliance, and write access only to the Compliance Ops ingestion role.
Remove any standing delete permission from operational users; deletion runs only through the approved destruction workflow.
Recertify access to the REG-002 archive every six months and remove leavers and role changers.
Log every access recertification result as evidence the archive is controlled.
checklist.done: archive access is least-privilege with no standing delete right, and recertification is completed and evidenced every six months.

checklist.step: Apply legal holds when an examination or dispute arises
actions: On notice of a rate examination, market conduct exam, department inquiry or rate-related litigation, identify the states, companies and effective-date range in scope.
Place a legal hold on every matching archive record so the destruction date is suspended.
Notify the Records Manager and Compliance Ops of the hold scope in writing and record the matter reference on the records.
Release the hold only on written instruction from General Counsel and record the release date.
checklist.done: every examination or dispute produces a scoped, recorded legal hold that suspends destruction until counsel releases it.

checklist.step: Run the monthly archive completeness sweep
actions: List every filing closed in SERFF in the last month and join it to the archive by SERFF tracking number.
Flag any closed filing with no archive record, and any archive record missing a disposition letter or approved rate pages.
Chase the responsible Regulatory Filing Specialist with a 5-business-day correction deadline.
Report the open gap count to the Head of Compliance monthly.
checklist.done: a monthly sweep identifies and closes archive gaps within 5 business days and the open gap count is reported.

checklist.step: Prove retrievability with a live retrieval drill
actions: Each quarter pick three filings at random - one current year, one three years old, one near the end of its retention window.
Ask a person who did not archive them to retrieve the complete pack using only the SERFF tracking number.
Time the retrieval and check the pack against the record definition checklist item by item.
Record the elapsed time and any missing component, and fix the index where retrieval was slow rather than merely noting it.
checklist.done: a quarterly drill retrieves three packs by tracking number alone, timed and checked against the record definition.

checklist.step: Assemble the examination pack on request
actions: On receiving a department document request from the Regulatory Affairs Manager, translate it into archive index keys - state, company, line, effective-date range.
Assemble the packs and produce a document index listing every item with its date and SERFF tracking number.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the pack for privilege and for anything responsive but not requested before it leaves.
Deliver inside the department's stated window and record what was produced and when.
checklist.done: each examination request is answered with an indexed, counsel-reviewed pack delivered inside the department's window and logged.

checklist.step: Review records reaching their destruction date
actions: Ninety days before a record's destruction date, confirm the rate version is genuinely withdrawn, no legal hold applies and no state rule requires longer retention.
Route the destruction list to Regulatory Counsel and the Head of Compliance for approval.
Destroy only approved records through the repository workflow and keep a permanent destruction certificate naming what was destroyed, when and under whose approval.
Never destroy on schedule alone where an examination cycle is open in the state.
checklist.done: no record is destroyed without a 90-day review, counsel and compliance approval, and a permanent destruction certificate.

checklist.step: Re-read the state retention rules annually
actions: Each year re-read the record-retention provisions in the rating and examination laws of the 51 jurisdictions, starting with the states whose exam cycles reach furthest back.
Compare the longest state requirement to the company's 7-year schedule and raise the schedule where a state is longer.
Record the review date, the states checked and any change to the retention period.
Instruct the Records Manager to relabel affected record classes where the period changes.
checklist.done: an annual dated retention review exists covering all 51 jurisdictions with any schedule change applied to existing records.

checklist.step: Report archive health to the Compliance Committee
actions: Report quarterly the archive completeness rate, open gaps by state, retrieval drill timings and any early-destruction or altered-record incident.
Report legal holds in force and the examinations driving them.
Record committee decisions and any accepted risk with an owner and a review date.
Track prior-quarter actions to closure before opening new ones.
checklist.done: a quarterly archive health report with completeness rate, retrieval timings, incidents and holds is minuted with owned actions.

testing.step: Build the population of filings requiring an archive record
actions: Export from SERFF every rate filing reaching a disposition in the quarter, with state, company, tracking number and disposition date.
Add filings withdrawn or disapproved, since those records are retained on the same basis as approvals.
Reconcile the export to the internal filing tracker's closed list and resolve every difference.
Sign the population as complete and record the export date.
testing.done: a reconciled population of dispositions requiring archive records exists, signed as complete.

testing.step: Join every disposition to an archive record
actions: Join the disposition population to the archive on SERFF tracking number.
List filings with no archive record and archive records with no matching disposition.
Measure the elapsed days from disposition date to ingestion date against the 10-business-day standard.
Treat any missing record as an automatic exception regardless of how recent the disposition is.
testing.done: every disposition is joined to an archive record with ingestion lag measured, and every gap is listed.

testing.step: Draw a current and an aged sample
actions: Take 20 records by seeded random selection from the quarter's dispositions.
Take a further 15 records spread across the prior seven years, at least one per year and weighted to the oldest years where migration losses occur.
Record the seed, the population sizes, the stratification and the selection date.
Confirm the combined sample covers at least six states and more than one writing company.
testing.done: a reproducible two-part sample covering the current quarter and each of the prior seven years is documented.

testing.step: Test each sampled record against the record definition
actions: Open each sampled record and check it item by item against the published record definition checklist.
Confirm the disposition letter and the approved rate pages are present - these two carry zero tolerance.
Confirm both the as-submitted and the as-approved package versions exist where objections changed the content.
List every missing component by record with the component name.
testing.done: each sampled record is checked component by component and every missing item is listed by name.

testing.step: Re-perform a blind retrieval by tracking number
actions: Using only the SERFF tracking number, retrieve each sampled record without help from Compliance Ops.
Time each retrieval and record any that could not be completed inside 5 business days.
Repeat the retrieval for three records using state, company and effective date instead, to test the alternate index keys an examiner is more likely to use.
Record failed or slow retrievals as index defects with the key that failed.
testing.done: every sampled record is independently retrievable inside 5 business days by tracking number and by state-company-date.

testing.step: Verify the archived documents match what the regulator holds
actions: For eight sampled records, open the corresponding filing in SERFF and compare the attachment list to the archived document list.
Compare the archived approved rate pages page by page against the copy in SERFF for two records.
Confirm the archived disposition letter is identical to the SERFF disposition.
Record any archived document that differs from the regulator's copy as a fail, since the archive is meant to be the regulator's record.
testing.done: archived documents are proven identical to the SERFF copies for the tested records, with any difference raised as a fail.

testing.step: Test retention labels, destruction dates and legal holds
actions: For each sampled record confirm a retention label is applied and the destruction date is computed from rate withdrawal, not from filing closure.
Cross-check the in-force rate version list and confirm no record for an in-force rate carries an active destruction date.
List records under legal hold and confirm their destruction dates are suspended and the matter reference is recorded.
Attempt an edit and a delete on one archived record with an operational user account and confirm both are refused.
testing.done: retention labels, withdrawal-based destruction dates and legal holds are verified, and edit and delete attempts are proven to fail.

testing.step: Test the destruction and access control history
actions: Pull the destruction log for the period and confirm every destroyed record had a completed 90-day review, counsel and compliance approval and a destruction certificate.
Recompute the destruction eligibility date for three destroyed records and confirm destruction did not precede it.
Pull the access recertification results for the REG-002 archive and confirm they were completed in the last six months with leavers removed.
Confirm no operational user holds a standing delete right.
testing.done: every destruction is supported by an approved review and certificate, and access recertification is current with no standing delete rights.

testing.step: Log every records exception with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one issue per exception with state, SERFF tracking number, the missing component or failed control, and whether the record can be reconstructed from SERFF.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: export not taken at closure, ingestion checklist bypassed, index key wrong, retention clock keyed to closure, hold not applied, access right too broad.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and require re-export from SERFF within 10 business days for any recoverable gap.
Escalate any record that cannot be reconstructed to the Head of Compliance for a written acceptance of the exposure.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and either a re-export commitment or a written exposure acceptance.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the records test
actions: Report the archive completeness rate for current and aged samples separately, plus retrieval timings and any early-destruction incident.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the blind retrieval results and the SERFF-to-archive comparison.
Have the independent reviewer, who archived none of the sampled records and performed the retrievals personally, sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper under REG-002 and report unreconstructable records and hold status to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, completeness rates, retrieval timings and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.
